uryankhay-krai.t: The Russian protectorate over Tuva established in 1914, which brought Russian settlers to the upper Yenisei and preceded the Tuvan People's Republic.
uryankhay-krai.o: [[e:tuva|Tuva]], called Uryankhay or Tannu Uriankhai, had been under the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] as part of its Mongolian frontier. After the [[e:qing-empire|Qing]] collapse in 1911, [[e:russia|Russia]], the [[s:bogd-khanate-of-mongolia|Bogd Khanate of Mongolia]] and [[e:china|China]] all claimed it. Some Tuvan nobles appealed to Russia, and in 1914 the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] declared a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]].
uryankhay-krai.r: The territory was administered by a Russian commissioner under the [[e:irkutsk|Irkutsk]] governor-general, alongside traditional Tuvan princes and Buddhist monasteries. Russian peasant settlement increased, and in 1914 the town of [[e:kyzyl|Belotsarsk]] (later Kyzyl) was founded as the administrative centre on the [[e:yenisei-river|Yenisei]]. The Tuvan herding economy was little changed.
uryankhay-krai.e: After 1917 Russian administration collapsed, and Red and White forces, Chinese troops and Mongolian forces fought over [[e:tuva|Tuva]]. With Soviet backing, Tuvan leaders proclaimed the [[s:tuvan-peoples-republic|Tuvan People's Republic]] in August 1921.

united-arab-republic.t: The union of Egypt and Syria under Gamal Abdel Nasser, the high point of pan-Arab nationalism.
united-arab-republic.o: Syrian officers and [[e:baath-party|Ba'athist]] politicians, alarmed by communist influence and inspired by [[e:gamal-abdel-nasser|Nasser's]] prestige after the 1956 [[e:suez-crisis|Suez crisis]], asked [[e:egypt|Egypt]] for union. On 1 February 1958 the United Arab Republic was proclaimed, with Nasser as president and [[e:cairo|Cairo]] as capital; a plebiscite confirmed it.
united-arab-republic.r: [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] became the northern region of a centralised state. Political parties were dissolved, including the [[e:baath-party|Ba'ath]], and Egyptian officials and security services dominated, with Field Marshal [[e:abdel-hakim-amer|Abdel Hakim Amer]] as [[e:gamal-abdel-nasser|Nasser's]] representative in [[e:damascus|Damascus]]. Land reform and the nationalisation of banks and industry in 1961 alienated Syrian landowners and merchants. A loose confederation with [[s:yemen-arab-republic|North Yemen]], the [[e:united-arab-states|United Arab States]], was also formed.
united-arab-republic.e: On 28 September 1961 Syrian officers seized power in [[e:damascus|Damascus]] and declared secession. [[e:egypt|Egypt]] kept the name United Arab Republic until 1971.

urusalim.t: Urusalim, the Canaanite city-state of Jerusalem, a small Egyptian vassal in the Amarna age that later became the capital of King David.
urusalim.o: [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] grew around the [[e:gihon-spring|Gihon]] spring on a ridge in the Judaean hills. Egyptian execration texts of the 19th century BCE mention Rushalimum, and in the [[e:middle-bronze-age|Middle Bronze Age]] its inhabitants built massive towers to protect the spring.
urusalim.r: In the 14th century BCE its ruler [[e:abdi-heba|Abdi-Heba]], a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]], wrote several [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]] complaining about rivals such as [[s:shechem|Shechem]] and asking for troops. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] calls the later inhabitants [[e:jebusites|Jebusites]] and the city Jebus. Its realm was a modest hill country territory.
urusalim.e: According to the [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]], [[e:david|David]] captured the city c. 1000 BCE and made it the capital of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]]. The Canaanite city thus became the centre of later Jewish, Christian and Islamic history.

ukrainian-peoples-republic.t: The Ukrainian national republic born in the Russian Revolution, which declared independence in 1918 and fought for its survival until 1921.
ukrainian-peoples-republic.o: In March 1917 Ukrainian parties formed the [[e:central-rada|Central Rada]] in [[e:kyiv|Kyiv]], chaired by the historian [[e:mykhailo-hrushevsky|Mykhailo Hrushevsky]]. After the [[e:october-revolution|October Revolution]] its [[e:third-universal|Third Universal]] of November 1917 proclaimed the Ukrainian People's Republic, and the [[e:fourth-universal|Fourth Universal]] of January 1918 declared full independence.
ukrainian-peoples-republic.r: The [[e:central-rada|Rada]] passed land reform and made a separate peace with the [[e:central-powers|Central Powers]] at [[e:treaty-of-brest-litovsk|Brest-Litovsk]] in February 1918, relying on German troops against the Bolsheviks. In April 1918 the Germans replaced it with the [[s:ukrainian-state|Ukrainian State]], but in December a [[e:directorate-of-ukraine|Directorate]] led by [[e:volodymyr-vynnychenko|Volodymyr Vynnychenko]] and [[e:symon-petliura|Symon Petliura]] restored the republic. In January 1919 it proclaimed union with the [[s:west-ukrainian-peoples-republic|West Ukrainian People's Republic]].
ukrainian-peoples-republic.e: Attacked by Bolsheviks, [[e:white-movement|Whites]] and [[e:poles|Poles]], the republic lost most of its territory in 1919. [[e:symon-petliura|Petliura]] allied with the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]] in 1920, but the [[e:peace-of-riga|Peace of Riga]] in 1921 divided [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]] between [[e:poland|Poland]] and the [[s:ukrainian-ssr|Ukrainian SSR]]. The government continued in exile until 1992.

union-of-south-africa.t: The self-governing British dominion that united four colonies in 1910 and laid the legal foundations of segregation and apartheid.
union-of-south-africa.o: After the [[e:second-boer-war|Second Boer War]], the [[s:cape-colony|Cape Colony]], the [[s:natal-colony|Natal Colony]], the [[s:transvaal-colony|Transvaal Colony]] and the [[s:orange-river-colony|Orange River Colony]] were united by the [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]] Act of 1909. The Union came into being on 31 May 1910, with [[e:louis-botha|Louis Botha]] as its first prime minister, [[e:pretoria|Pretoria]] as administrative capital and [[e:cape-town|Cape Town]] as legislative capital.
union-of-south-africa.r: Political power was reserved almost entirely for whites. The [[e:natives-land-act-1913|Natives Land Act]] of 1913 restricted African land ownership to reserves, and the [[e:african-national-congress|African National Congress]], founded in 1912 to defend African rights, campaigned against it. [[s:republic-of-south-africa|South Africa]] fought in both world wars under [[e:louis-botha|Botha]] and [[e:jan-smuts|Jan Smuts]] and gained full [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] through the [[e:statute-of-westminster-1931|Statute of Westminster]] in 1931. In 1948 the [[e:national-party-south-africa|National Party]] of [[e:d-f-malan|D. F. Malan]] won power and built apartheid.
union-of-south-africa.e: After a narrow whites-only referendum in 1960, held under Prime Minister [[e:hendrik-verwoerd|Hendrik Verwoerd]], the Union became the [[s:republic-of-south-africa|Republic of South Africa]] on 31 May 1961 and left the [[e:commonwealth-of-nations|Commonwealth]], whose members criticised apartheid.

ursum.t: Ursum, a north Syrian city on the caravan routes to Anatolia, remembered for its long siege by the Hittite king Hattusili I.
ursum.o: [[e:urshu|Urshu]] lay west of the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]], probably near modern [[e:gaziantep|Gaziantep]], on the routes between [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]]. It appears in Old Assyrian trade letters and the [[s:mari|Mari]] archives as a city with its own king and a place where merchants traded.
ursum.r: Little is known of its government. The [[s:mari|Mari]] letters show it linked to the [[s:kingdom-of-upper-mesopotamia|Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia]] and [[s:yamhad|Yamhad]] in the politics of the 18th century BCE.
ursum.e: In the 17th century BCE [[e:hattusili-i|Hattusili I]] of the [[s:hittite-empire|Hittite Empire]] besieged Ursum for months. A Hittite literary text, the [[e:siege-of-urshu|Siege of Urshu]], mocks his generals' failures. The city fell and lost its independence.

united-baltic-duchy.t: Short-lived German client state proclaimed by Baltic German nobles in late 1918, meant to unite Estonia and Livonia under a German duke.
united-baltic-duchy.o: During the German occupation of 1918, [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] nobles sought to keep their dominance. Councils dominated by them asked for a union with [[e:germany|Germany]], and on 5 November 1918 a United Baltic Duchy was proclaimed in Riga, covering the former [[s:governorate-of-estonia|Governorate of Estonia]] and [[s:governorate-of-livonia|Governorate of Livonia]], with the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia-1918|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]] (1918) to join.
united-baltic-duchy.r: [[e:duke-adolf-friedrich-of-mecklenburg|Duke Adolf Friedrich of Mecklenburg]] was chosen as head of state but never took office. A regency council under Baron Adolf Pilar von Pilchau governed in name only, relying entirely on German troops. [[e:latvians|Latvians]] and [[e:estonians|Estonians]], who were the great majority of the population, rejected the state.
united-baltic-duchy.e: [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat in the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] doomed the duchy. The regency council dissolved itself on 28 November 1918, and its territory passed to the [[s:republic-of-estonia|Republic of Estonia]] and the [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]], amid fighting with Soviet forces. [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] volunteers later fought in the [[e:baltic-landeswehr|Landeswehr]].

united-kingdom-of-portugal-brazil-and-th.t: A transatlantic monarchy ruled from Rio de Janeiro, created when Brazil was raised to a kingdom equal to Portugal in 1815.
united-kingdom-of-portugal-brazil-and-th.o: Fleeing [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] invasion, the Portuguese court sailed to [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] in 1807-1808 and settled in [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]]. On 16 December 1815 the [[e:john-vi-of-portugal|Prince Regent John]] raised [[e:brazil|Brazil]] from colony to the [[s:kingdom-of-brazil|Kingdom of Brazil]], uniting it with the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-algarve|Kingdom of the Algarve]].
united-kingdom-of-portugal-brazil-and-th.r: [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio]] became the seat of government of a global empire, with new ministries, a royal library, a bank and opened ports. [[e:john-vi-of-portugal|John VI]], acclaimed king in 1818 after the death of Maria I, stayed in [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]], while Portugal was governed by a regency under strong British influence and resented its subordinate status.
united-kingdom-of-portugal-brazil-and-th.e: The [[e:liberal-revolution-of-1820|Liberal Revolution]] in [[e:porto|Porto]] in 1820 forced [[e:john-vi-of-portugal|John VI]] to return to [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]] in 1821, leaving his son Pedro as regent. When the [[e:portuguese-constituent-cortes|Lisbon Cortes]] tried to reduce [[e:brazil|Brazil's]] status, Pedro declared independence on 7 September 1822, founding the [[s:brazilian-empire|Brazilian Empire]].

united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.t: The revolutionary state formed in Buenos Aires in 1810 that declared independence from Spain in 1816 and became the core of Argentina.
united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.o: The May Revolution of 25 May 1810 replaced the [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] of the [[s:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata]] with a [[e:primera-junta|Primera Junta]] in [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]]. Armies were sent to spread the revolution, but [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]] and [[s:royal-audiencia-of-charcas|Upper Peru]] resisted, and [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]] held out for [[e:spain|Spain]] until 1814.
united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.r: Government passed from juntas to triumvirates and, from 1814, Supreme Directors. [[e:manuel-belgrano|Manuel Belgrano]] created the blue and white flag in 1812, and the [[e:assembly-of-the-year-xiii|Assembly of the Year XIII]] abolished titles and freed children born to enslaved mothers. The [[e:congress-of-tucuman|Congress of Tucumán]] declared independence on 9 July 1816. [[e:jose-de-san-martin|José de San Martín's]] [[e:army-of-the-andes|Army of the Andes]] liberated [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] in 1817 and 1818. Conflict between [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] and federalist provinces, such as those of the [[s:federal-league|Federal League]], was constant.
united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.e: After the [[e:battle-of-cepeda-1820|Battle of Cepeda]] in 1820 central government collapsed. [[e:bernardino-rivadavia|Bernardino Rivadavia's]] presidency and a war with [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] over [[s:cisplatina|Cisplatina]] followed. The [[e:federal-pact|Federal Pact]] of 1831 created the [[s:argentine-confederation|Argentine Confederation]].

united-provinces-of-central-italy.t: A short-lived union of Tuscany, Modena, Parma and Romagna formed in 1859, which voted to join Piedmont and paved the way for Italian unity.
united-provinces-of-central-italy.o: During the war of 1859 between [[e:austria|Austria]] and the alliance of [[e:france|France]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], the rulers of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Grand Duchy of Tuscany]], the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]] and the [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Duchy of Parma and Piacenza]] fled, and the papal [[e:romagna|Legations of Romagna]] rebelled. Their provisional governments formed a league with a common army under General [[e:manfredo-fanti|Manfredo Fanti]].
united-provinces-of-central-italy.r: The union was a military and political alliance rather than a full state. [[e:luigi-carlo-farini|Luigi Carlo Farini]] governed [[e:modena|Modena]], [[s:duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza|Parma]] and [[e:romagna|Romagna]], united as [[e:emilia|Emilia]], while [[e:bettino-ricasoli|Bettino Ricasoli]] led [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]]. Their assemblies voted to join the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], defying the [[e:armistice-of-villafranca|Peace of Villafranca]], which had foreseen the return of the old rulers.
united-provinces-of-central-italy.e: After plebiscites in March 1860, the territories were annexed to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]], with [[e:france|France]] receiving [[e:nice|Nice]] and [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Savoy]] in exchange. They became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-italy|Kingdom of Italy]] in 1861.

uruk.t: The great city of the Uruk period, where writing was invented around 3300 BCE, and the seat of the legendary king Gilgamesh.
uruk.o: Uruk grew from two [[e:ubaid-period|Ubaid-period]] villages, [[e:kullaba|Kullaba]] and [[e:eanna|Eanna]], into the largest city in the world by about 3500 to 3100 BCE, with perhaps 40,000 inhabitants inside walls later credited to [[e:gilgamesh|Gilgamesh]]. Its expansion gave its name to the [[e:uruk-period|Uruk period]], when Uruk-style pottery and colonies spread up the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] into [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[e:iran|Iran]].
uruk.r: Huge temple precincts dedicated to [[e:inanna|Inanna]] in the [[e:eanna|Eanna]] district and to the sky god An dominated the city. The earliest proto-[[e:cuneiform|cuneiform]] tablets, mostly administrative records of grain, livestock and labour, come from Eanna, along with cylinder seals and the [[e:warka-vase|Warka Vase]]. In the [[e:early-dynastic-period|Early Dynastic period]] kings such as [[e:enmerkar|Enmerkar]], [[e:lugalbanda|Lugalbanda]] and [[e:gilgamesh|Gilgamesh]] were remembered in epic, and [[e:lugal-zage-si|Lugal-zage-si of Umma]] made Uruk his capital when he united [[e:sumer|Sumer]].
uruk.e: Uruk fell to the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]], but [[e:utu-hengal|Utu-hengal]] of Uruk expelled the [[s:gutian-rule|Gutians]] around 2119 BCE. Independent again under the dynasty of [[e:sin-kashid|Sin-kashid]], it was conquered by [[e:rim-sin-i|Rim-Sin]] of [[s:larsa|Larsa]] in 1802 BCE. The city itself lived on as a temple centre into [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] and Parthian times and was abandoned only around the 7th century CE.

upper-canada.t: The English-speaking British colony founded for Loyalists north of the Great Lakes, forerunner of the province of Ontario.
upper-canada.o: The [[e:constitutional-act-1791|Constitutional Act]] of 1791 split the [[s:province-of-quebec|Province of Quebec]], creating Upper [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] upriver from [[e:montreal|Montreal]] for the Loyalists who had settled there after the [[e:american-revolution|American Revolution]]. Its first lieutenant governor, [[e:john-graves-simcoe|John Graves Simcoe]], laid out roads and moved the capital from [[e:niagara-on-the-lake|Newark]] to York, the future [[e:toronto|Toronto]], in 1796.
upper-canada.r: Upper [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] had English [[e:common-law|common law]], freehold [[e:land-tenure|land tenure]] and an elected assembly, but power lay with the lieutenant governor and an appointed elite known as the Family Compact. Land set aside as clergy reserves for the [[e:church-of-england|Church of England]] was a long-standing grievance. The colony repulsed American invasions in the [[e:war-of-1812|War of 1812]], and British immigration greatly increased its population after 1815.
upper-canada.e: Reformers led by [[e:william-lyon-mackenzie|William Lyon Mackenzie]] rose in a brief rebellion in 1837. Following [[e:john-lambton-1st-earl-of-durham|Lord Durham's]] report, Upper [[s:province-of-canada|Canada]] was merged with [[s:lower-canada|Lower Canada]] in 1841 as the Province of [[e:canada|Canada]]; it re-emerged as [[e:ontario|Ontario]] at Confederation in 1867.

uesugi-clan-domain.t: The Echigo domain of Uesugi Kenshin, the warrior lord famed for his rivalry with Takeda Shingen and his devotion to the war god Bishamonten.
uesugi-clan-domain.o: The [[e:nagao-clan|Nagao]] family were deputies of the Uesugi governors of [[e:echigo-province|Echigo]]. [[e:uesugi-kenshin|Nagao Kagetora]], later Uesugi Kenshin, took over the clan in 1548 and secured the province by about 1551, ruling from [[e:kasugayama-castle|Kasugayama]] castle. In 1561 the fugitive [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]] deputy [[e:uesugi-norimasa|Uesugi Norimasa]] adopted him, giving him the Uesugi name and office.
uesugi-clan-domain.r: [[e:uesugi-kenshin|Kenshin]] campaigned almost every year, in the [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]] against the Later Hojo and in [[e:shinano-province|Shinano]] against [[e:takeda-shingen|Takeda Shingen]], with five battles at [[e:battles-of-kawanakajima|Kawanakajima]], and later in [[e:etchu-province|Etchu]] and [[e:noto-province|Noto]]. [[e:echigo-province|Echigo]]'s trade in ramie cloth and gold and [[e:silver|silver]] mines funded his wars. He defeated an [[e:oda-clan|Oda]] army at [[e:battle-of-tedorigawa|Tedorigawa]] in 1577.
uesugi-clan-domain.e: [[e:uesugi-kenshin|Kenshin]] died in 1578; his adopted son [[e:uesugi-kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] won the succession war and served [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]], who moved him to [[e:aizu|Aizu]] in 1598. After opposing [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] in 1600 his lands were cut to the [[s:yonezawa-domain|Yonezawa Domain]].

usfurid-dynasty.t: A Bedouin dynasty of the Banu Uqayl that replaced the Uyunids in eastern Arabia and controlled the al-Ahsa oasis in the 13th and 14th centuries.
usfurid-dynasty.o: The Usfurids, named after their ancestor Usfur ibn Rashid, were a clan of the [[e:banu-amir|Banu Amir]] branch of the [[s:uqaylid-dynasty|Banu Uqayl]] tribe. Around 1253 they took [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Ahsa]] from the weakened [[s:uyunid-emirate|Uyunid Emirate]] and became the leading power of eastern [[e:arabia|Arabia]].
usfurid-dynasty.r: Their power rested on [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] tribal forces and on the revenues of the date oases and the pilgrimage and trade routes between [[e:iraq|Iraq]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]]. They maintained links with the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]] in Iraq and [[e:iran|Iran]] and competed with the [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Kingdom of Ormus]] for control of the [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] islands and the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] ports. Sources on them are thin.
usfurid-dynasty.e: In the early 14th century the Usfurids lost the islands and [[e:qatif|Qatif]] to rulers allied with [[s:kingdom-of-ormus|Hormuz]], and by about 1330 their authority had passed to the [[s:jarwanid-dynasty|Jarwanid dynasty]] and other local leaders.

urkesh.t: Urkesh, a Hurrian city-kingdom in north-eastern Syria, revered in myth as the home of the god Kumarbi and ruled by kings with the title endan.
urkesh.o: Urkesh grew at Tell Mozan in the foothills of the [[e:taurus-mountains|Taurus]] mountains, controlling access to the [[e:copper|copper]] of the Anatolian highlands. By the mid-3rd millennium BCE it was the main political and religious centre of the [[e:hurrians|Hurrians]], a people who spoke a language unrelated to the Semitic tongues of their neighbours.
urkesh.r: Its rulers bore the Hurrian title endan. Excavations led by Giorgio and Marilyn Buccellati since 1984 uncovered the palace of King Tupkish and Queen Uqnitum, a great temple terrace and a deep ritual pit used to summon underworld spirits. A daughter of [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin]] of the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]], Tar'am-Agade, lived there, probably as a royal bride.
urkesh.e: Urkesh lost importance in the early 2nd millennium BCE, appearing in the [[s:mari|Mari]] letters as a minor kingdom. It survived as a religious centre under the [[s:mitanni-empire|Mitanni Empire]] before being largely abandoned in the 14th century BCE, though Hurrian myths kept its name alive.

uxmal.t: The leading city of the Puuc hills of Yucatán, celebrated for the refined mosaic architecture of the Nunnery Quadrangle and the Governor's Palace.
uxmal.o: Uxmal grew in the hilly [[e:puuc|Puuc]] region of western [[e:yucatan-peninsula|Yucatán]], where fertile soils supported farming despite the lack of surface water. Cisterns (chultunes) stored rainwater. The city became powerful in the 8th century and reached its height around 850-925.
uxmal.r: Its buildings show [[e:puuc|Puuc]] style at its finest: smooth lower walls and upper façades of carved stone mosaic, with masks of the rain god [[e:chaac|Chaak]], latticework and serpents. The [[e:pyramid-of-the-magician|Pyramid of the Magician]], the [[e:nunnery-quadrangle|Nunnery Quadrangle]] and the [[e:governors-palace-uxmal|Governor's Palace]] dominate the site. A ruler known as [[e:lord-chak|Lord Chak]], active around 900, appears to have built many of them. Causeways linked Uxmal with [[e:kabah|Kabah]] and Nohpat, suggesting a regional state.
uxmal.e: Uxmal declined after about 1000, probably as [[s:chichen-itza|Chichen Itza]] rose. The [[e:tutul-xiu|Xiu]] lineage, later rulers of [[s:mani|Maní]], claimed connections with it. It became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1996.

ustrushana.t: A mountain principality between Samarkand and Ferghana whose Afshin rulers rose to command the armies of the Abbasid caliphate.
ustrushana.o: Ustrushana lay along the upper [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]] and the Turkestan range, around the town of [[e:bunjikat|Bunjikat]] near modern [[e:istaravshan|Istaravshan]]. Its rulers, who bore the title afshin, emerged in the 7th century as Sogdian-speaking lords in the zone of the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]].
ustrushana.r: Excavations at [[e:bunjikat|Bunjikat]] and Shahristan revealed palaces with wall paintings, including an image of a she-wolf suckling twins. The afshins long resisted Arab conquest, submitting to the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliph]] [[e:al-mamun|al-Ma'mun]] only around 822. The afshin [[e:al-afshin|Khaydhar ibn Kawus]] became a top general for [[e:al-mutasim|al-Mu'tasim]], crushing the revolt of [[e:babak-khorramdin|Babak Khorramdin]], before being tried for heresy and dying in prison in 841.
ustrushana.e: The afshins continued as local governors under Abbasid and [[e:samanid-empire|Samanid]] authority until 893, when the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]]'s [[e:ismail-ibn-ahmad|Isma'il ibn Ahmad]] ended their dynasty and absorbed Ustrushana.

uganda.t: An East African republic built around the old Great Lakes kingdoms, whose post-independence turmoil under Obote and Amin gave way to Museveni's long rule.
uganda.o: The [[s:uganda-protectorate|Uganda Protectorate]] became independent on 9 October 1962 under Prime Minister [[e:milton-obote|Milton Obote]], with the kingdoms, above all the [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Kingdom of Buganda]], keeping federal status. [[e:mutesa-ii-of-buganda|Kabaka Mutesa II]] became ceremonial president in 1963.
uganda.r: In 1966 [[e:milton-obote|Obote]] suspended the constitution, attacked the [[e:kabaka-of-buganda|Kabaka's]] palace and in 1967 abolished the kingdoms. [[e:idi-amin|Idi Amin]] seized power in 1971, expelled the Asian community in 1972, and his regime killed an estimated 100,000 or more people. His invasion of [[s:tanzania|Tanzania]] led to his overthrow in 1979. Obote's second government faced the [[e:ugandan-bush-war|Bush War]], which brought [[e:yoweri-museveni|Yoweri Museveni's]] [[e:national-resistance-army|National Resistance Army]] to power in 1986.
uganda.e: Under [[e:yoweri-museveni|Museveni]], Uganda regained stability in most regions, restored the kingdoms as cultural institutions in 1993 and grew its economy, but also fought the [[e:lords-resistance-army|Lord's Resistance Army]] in the north and saw term limits removed. It remains a republic with [[e:kampala|Kampala]] as capital.

ugandi.t: Ancient Estonian county of the south-east, centred on the hillforts of Otepää and Tartu, which fought Rus' and the German crusaders before falling in 1224.
ugandi.o: Ugandi, in what is now south-eastern [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]], was one of the larger Estonian lands of the late [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], a union of parishes defended by hillforts. Its position on routes to [[e:pskov|Pskov]] and [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]] drew Rus' attention early: [[e:yaroslav-the-wise|Yaroslav the Wise]] of [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] captured [[e:tartu|Tartu]] around 1030 and briefly held it as Yuryev.
ugandi.r: Ugandi was governed by elders of its districts, who met to decide on war and tribute. Its people grew grain, kept [[e:cattle|cattle]] and traded with Rus' and the [[e:latgalians|Latgalians]] to the south. [[e:otepaa|Otepää]], whose name means 'bear's head', was its main stronghold, and [[e:tartu|Tartu]] on the Emajõgi river guarded the waterway east to [[e:lake-peipus|Lake Peipus]].
ugandi.e: From 1208 the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]] and their [[e:latgalians|Latgalian]] allies raided Ugandi, and [[e:otepaa|Otepää]] changed hands several times. When [[e:tartu|Tartu]] fell in 1224, after a siege in which the Rus' prince [[e:vyachko|Vyachko]] was killed, the conquest was complete. Ugandi became the core of the [[s:bishopric-of-dorpat|Bishopric of Dorpat]].

united-states.t: A federal republic founded by thirteen British colonies in 1776 that grew across North America to become the world's leading economic and military power.
united-states.o: Disputes over taxation and self-government led the thirteen colonies, from the [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Province of Massachusetts Bay]] to the [[s:province-of-georgia|Province of Georgia]], into war with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] in 1775. The [[e:united-states-declaration-of-independence|Declaration of Independence]] of 4 July 1776 proclaimed the United States, and the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1783|Treaty of Paris]] of 1783 secured independence and land to the [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]]. The Constitution of 1787 replaced the weak [[e:articles-of-confederation|Articles of Confederation]].
united-states.r: The Constitution created a federal system with separated powers and a [[e:united-states-bill-of-rights|Bill of Rights]]. The country expanded through the [[e:louisiana-purchase|Louisiana Purchase]], the annexation of the [[s:republic-of-texas|Republic of Texas]] and war with [[s:mexico|Mexico]], dispossessing Native nations. [[e:slavery|Slavery]] split North and South; the Civil War against the [[s:confederate-states-of-america|Confederate States of America]] ended it in 1865. Industrialisation and mass immigration followed.
united-states.e: Victory in the two world wars made the United States a superpower, and after the [[e:cold-war|Cold War]] it was the sole one. Women's suffrage in 1920 and the civil rights movement of the 1950s and 1960s widened democracy. It remains a federal republic of 50 states.

united-states-of-colombia.t: A radically federal Colombian republic of nine sovereign states, created by the Liberals in 1863 and ended by the centralist constitution of 1886.
united-states-of-colombia.o: After winning the civil war of 1860 to 1862 against the [[s:granadine-confederation|Granadine Confederation]], [[e:tomas-cipriano-de-mosquera|Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera]] and the Liberals met at [[e:rionegro|Rionegro]] in [[e:antioquia-department|Antioquia]] and adopted a new constitution in 1863, creating the [[e:united-states|United States]] of [[s:republic-of-colombia|Colombia]], made up of nine sovereign states including [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]].
united-states-of-colombia.r: The [[e:rionegro|Rionegro]] constitution gave the states their own armies and laws, limited the president to a two-year term and guaranteed broad freedoms, including freedom of the press and of trade in arms. The Radical Liberals separated church and state and promoted secular public schools. The weak central government struggled with frequent regional civil wars, notably the church-backed war of 1876 and 1877.
united-states-of-colombia.e: [[e:rafael-nunez|Rafael Núñez]] led a movement called the [[e:regeneration-colombia|Regeneration]]. After the civil war of 1885, the constitution of 1886 restored a centralised [[s:republic-of-colombia|Republic of Colombia]] with strong ties to the Catholic Church.

ulus-of-shiban.t: The appanage of Jochi's son Shiban in western Siberia and the southern Urals, from which the Shaybanid dynasties of Bukhara and Khiva descended.
ulus-of-shiban.o: [[e:shiban|Shiban]], a son of Jochi, distinguished himself in [[e:batu-khan|Batu]]'s western campaign of the late 1230s. In reward he received pastures east of the [[e:ural-mountains|Urals]], in the region of the [[e:tobol-river|Tobol]], [[e:tura-river|Tura]] and [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]], as an [[e:appanage|appanage]] within the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]].
ulus-of-shiban.r: The [[e:shaybanids|Shibanids]] ruled nomadic [[e:kipchaks|Kipchak]] and Mongol tribes and Siberian forest peoples, collecting [[e:fur-trade|furs]], with [[e:tyumen|Chimgi-Tura]] (later Tyumen) as a seat. They acted as junior members of the [[e:jochids|Jochid]] house, taking part in the [[e:golden-horde|Golden Horde's]] politics and civil wars in the 14th century, when several Shibanid princes claimed the throne at [[e:sarai|Sarai]].
ulus-of-shiban.e: As the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] collapsed, the [[e:shaybanids|Shibanid]] [[e:abul-khayr-khan|Abu'l-Khayr Khan]] proclaimed himself khan in 1428, founding the [[s:uzbek-khanate|Uzbek Khanate]]. Other Shibanids founded the [[s:tyumen-khanate|Tyumen Khanate]]. Abu'l-Khayr's grandson [[e:muhammad-shaybani|Muhammad Shaybani]] later conquered [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]], establishing the [[s:khanate-of-bukhara|Khanate of Bukhara]].

utica.t: One of the oldest Phoenician cities in North Africa, an ally and rival of Carthage that later became Rome's first African capital.
utica.o: Utica stood at the mouth of the [[e:medjerda|Bagradas]] (Medjerda) river, north-west of [[e:carthage|Carthage]]. Ancient writers such as [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny the Elder]] dated its foundation by [[e:phoenicians|Phoenicians]] from [[s:tyre|Tyre]] to 1101 BCE, making it older than Carthage. Archaeology has so far found remains only from about the 8th century BCE, so the traditional date is debated.
utica.r: Utica was a self-governing Punic city with its own magistrates ([[e:suffete|suffetes]]) and harbour, trading in grain, [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and fish. It became an ally of [[e:carthage|Carthage]] and part of the [[s:punic-empire|Punic Empire]] but often kept its distance, joining the rebels in the [[e:mercenary-war|Mercenary War]] of 240 to 238 BCE. Its gods were the Phoenician [[e:baal|Baal]] and [[e:tanit|Tanit]].
utica.e: In the [[e:third-punic-war|Third Punic War]] Utica sided with [[e:rome|Rome]], which made it a free city and the capital of the new province of [[e:africa|Africa]]. [[e:cato-the-younger|Cato the Younger]] killed himself there in 46 BCE after [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]]'s victory at [[e:battle-of-thapsus|Thapsus]], and the city merged into [[s:africa-proconsularis|Africa Proconsularis]]. The silting of the [[e:medjerda|Medjerda]] later left its ruins inland.

ukrainian-state.t: Hetman Pavlo Skoropadsky's conservative Ukrainian monarchy of 1918, installed with German backing, which founded Ukraine's Academy of Sciences.
ukrainian-state.o: On 29 April 1918 German occupation authorities, unhappy with the socialist [[e:central-rada|Central Rada]] of the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]], supported a coup by General [[e:pavlo-skoropadsky|Pavlo Skoropadsky]]. A congress of landowners proclaimed him [[e:hetman|hetman]], reviving the title of the [[s:cossack-hetmanate|Cossack Hetmanate]], and the state was renamed the Ukrainian State.
ukrainian-state.r: [[e:pavlo-skoropadsky|Skoropadsky]] ruled with broad powers and a cabinet of largely Russian-educated officials. He restored private property in land, angering peasants, and depended on German troops. Yet the state built a working administration and founded the [[e:national-academy-of-sciences-of-ukraine|Ukrainian Academy of Sciences]], a national library and new universities in [[e:kyiv|Kyiv]] and [[e:kamianets-podilskyi|Kamianets-Podilskyi]].
ukrainian-state.e: When [[e:germany|Germany]] collapsed in November 1918, [[e:pavlo-skoropadsky|Skoropadsky]] declared federation with a future non-Bolshevik [[e:russia|Russia]]. A revolt led by the [[e:directorate-of-ukraine|Directorate]] gathered strength, and on 14 December 1918 he abdicated and fled to Germany. The Directorate restored the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]].

united-tribes-of-new-zealand.t: A confederation of northern Māori chiefs who declared New Zealand's independence in 1835, five years before the Treaty of Waitangi.
united-tribes-of-new-zealand.o: The British Resident, [[e:james-busby|James Busby]], encouraged northern chiefs to choose a national flag in 1834 so that [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]]-built ships could be registered. In 1835, alarmed by the French adventurer [[e:charles-de-thierry|Charles de Thierry's]] claim to [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]], Busby gathered 34 chiefs at [[e:waitangi-northland|Waitangi]] to sign [[e:declaration-of-the-independence-of-new-zealand|He Whakaputanga]], the Declaration of Independence of [[e:new-zealand|New Zealand]], on 28 October.
united-tribes-of-new-zealand.r: The declaration vested sovereign power in the hereditary chiefs collectively and proposed an annual congress at [[e:waitangi-northland|Waitangi]] to make laws, with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] asked to act as protector. The congress never met, and the confederation existed mainly on paper and in its flag. By 1839 the number of signatories had grown to 52, including the [[e:waikato|Waikato]] chief [[e:potatau-te-wherowhero|Te Wherowhero]].
united-tribes-of-new-zealand.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], which had acknowledged the declaration, negotiated the [[e:treaty-of-waitangi|Treaty of Waitangi]] with the chiefs in 1840 and established the [[s:colony-of-new-zealand|Colony of New Zealand]]. Whether the treaty transferred the [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] the declaration asserted remains central to debate in [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]].

umma.t: The Sumerian city-state whose century-long border war with Lagash is the first conflict recorded in history, and home of Lugal-zage-si.
umma.o: Umma, modern Tell Jokha, lay on a canal north-west of [[s:lagash|Lagash]] and rose in the [[e:early-dynastic-period|Early Dynastic period]]. Its rulers clashed with [[e:lagash|Lagash]] over the fertile Gu-edena plain, a dispute that [[e:mesalim-of-kish|Mesalim of Kish]] tried to settle by setting up a boundary stone around 2600 BCE.
umma.r: The city's god was [[e:shara|Shara]], and its economy rested on irrigated barley, herds and textile work. The war with [[s:lagash|Lagash]] is told from the [[e:lagash|Lagash]] side, notably on [[e:eannatum|Eannatum's]] [[e:stele-of-the-vultures|Stele of the Vultures]] and in the inscriptions of [[e:enmetena|Enmetena]], which describe Umma breaking treaties and seizing land. Under [[e:lugal-zage-si|Lugal-zage-si]] Umma finally triumphed: he sacked Lagash, took [[s:uruk|Uruk]] as his capital and claimed rule from the Lower to the Upper Sea.
umma.e: [[e:sargon-of-akkad|Sargon of Akkad]] defeated [[e:lugal-zage-si|Lugal-zage-si]] around 2334 BCE and absorbed Umma into the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]]. Under the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]] it became a provincial centre whose tens of thousands of administrative tablets are a major source on [[e:third-dynasty-of-ur|Ur III]] government.

united-state-of-rajasthan.t: The union through which the princely states of Rajputana were merged, step by step, into the Indian state of Rajasthan between 1948 and 1950.
united-state-of-rajasthan.o: In March 1948 the states of south-eastern [[e:rajputana|Rajputana]], including Kota, [[s:bundi-state|Bundi]] and [[s:jhalawar-state|Jhalawar State]], formed the [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]] Union. [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] joined in April 1948, creating the United State of Rajasthan, and in March 1949 [[e:jaipur|Jaipur]], [[e:jodhpur|Jodhpur]], [[s:bikaner-state|Bikaner]] and [[s:jaisalmer-state|Jaisalmer]] joined to form [[e:united-state-of-greater-rajasthan|Greater Rajasthan]], with Jaipur as capital.
united-state-of-rajasthan.r: The [[e:maharana|Maharana of Udaipur]], [[e:bhupal-singh-of-udaipur|Bhupal Singh]], held the senior title of Maharajpramukh, and [[e:man-singh-ii-of-jaipur|Man Singh II of Jaipur]] became [[e:rajpramukh|Rajpramukh]]. Elected ministers under [[e:hiralal-shastri|Hiralal Shastri]] formed the government. The [[s:matsya-union|Matsya Union]] joined in May 1949, bringing in [[s:alwar-state|Alwar]], [[s:bharatpur-state|Bharatpur]], [[s:dholpur-state|Dholpur]] and [[s:karauli-state|Karauli]].
united-state-of-rajasthan.e: With the inclusion of [[s:sirohi-state|Sirohi]] and the adoption of the Constitution in January 1950, the union became the state of [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]]. [[e:ajmer|Ajmer]] and further territories were added in 1956.

united-states-army-military-government-i.t: The American military government that ruled Korea south of the 38th parallel from 1945 until the founding of the Republic of Korea in 1948.
united-states-army-military-government-i.o: Under the agreement dividing [[e:korea|Korea]] at the 38th parallel, the [[e:xxiv-corps-united-states|US XXIV Corps]] under Lieutenant General [[e:john-r-hodge|John R. Hodge]] landed at [[e:incheon|Incheon]] on 8 September 1945 and accepted the Japanese surrender in [[e:seoul|Seoul]]. The occupation set up a military government with General [[e:archibald-v-arnold|Archibald Arnold]] as first governor.
united-states-army-military-government-i.r: Lacking knowledge of [[e:korea|Korea]], the Americans refused to recognise either the [[s:peoples-republic-of-korea|People's Republic of Korea]] or the exiled Provisional Government and initially kept Japanese-era officials and police. The [[e:moscow|Moscow]] Conference's plan for a trusteeship provoked furious protests, and joint talks with the [[e:soviet-union|Soviets]] failed. [[e:rice|Rice]] shortages, strikes and the Autumn Uprising of 1946 met harsh repression, while right-wing politicians such as [[e:syngman-rhee|Syngman Rhee]] gained ground.
united-states-army-military-government-i.e: The [[s:united-states|United States]] took the Korean question to the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]], which supervised elections in the south in May 1948, amid the [[e:jeju-island|Jeju]] uprising. The [[e:south-korea|Republic of Korea]] was proclaimed on 15 August 1948 under [[e:syngman-rhee|Syngman Rhee]].

united-principalities.t: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia under one prince that created the modern Romanian state and won its independence from the Ottomans.
united-principalities.o: After the [[e:crimean-war|Crimean War]] the [[e:paris|Paris]] settlement allowed [[s:principality-of-moldavia|Moldavia]] and [[s:principality-of-wallachia|Wallachia]] separate assemblies under a common commission. Exploiting a loophole, both assemblies elected the same man, [[e:alexandru-ioan-cuza|Alexandru Ioan Cuza]], as prince in January and February 1859. The personal union became a single state with one government and parliament in [[e:bucharest|Bucharest]] in 1862, taking the name [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]].
united-principalities.r: [[e:alexandru-ioan-cuza|Cuza]] secularised the vast monastery estates in 1863, carried out a land reform in 1864, introduced a civil code and founded the universities of Iași and [[e:bucharest|Bucharest]]. His authoritarian methods provoked a coup in 1866, and [[e:carol-i-of-romania|Carol]] of [[s:principality-of-hohenzollern-sigmaringen|Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen]] was installed as prince under a liberal constitution modelled on [[e:belgium|Belgium's]]. Grain exports through [[e:galati|Galați]] and [[e:braila|Brăila]] drove the economy.
united-principalities.e: [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]] declared independence in 1877 and fought alongside [[e:russia|Russia]] against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]]. The [[e:congress-of-berlin|Congress of Berlin]] in 1878 recognised independence, adding [[e:northern-dobruja|Northern Dobruja]] but returning southern [[e:bessarabia|Bessarabia]] to Russia. In 1881 [[e:carol-i-of-romania|Carol]] was crowned king, founding the Kingdom of [[e:romania|Romania]].

utpala-dynasty.t: The Kashmir dynasty of Avantivarman, whose engineer Suyya tamed the Jhelum and whose court fostered great Sanskrit literary theory.
utpala-dynasty.o: In 855 [[e:avantivarman|Avantivarman]], a grandson of a minister of the [[s:karkota-dynasty|Karkota dynasty]], took the throne of [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] with the support of powerful ministers, founding a new dynasty after a period of weak Karkota rule. The main source for the dynasty is [[e:rajatarangini|Kalhana's Rajatarangini]].
utpala-dynasty.r: [[e:avantivarman|Avantivarman's]] minister [[e:suyya|Suyya]] cleared rocks from the [[e:jhelum|Jhelum]], drained marshes and built embankments, increasing [[e:rice|rice]] production and lowering grain prices, as [[e:kalhana|Kalhana]] records. The king built the temples of [[e:avantipur|Avantipur]], and the critic [[e:anandavardhana|Anandavardhana]] wrote the [[e:dhvanyaloka|Dhvanyaloka]], a founding text of Indian aesthetics, during his reign. His son Shankaravarman campaigned in the [[e:punjab|Punjab]] but became notorious for heavy taxation and plunder of temples.
utpala-dynasty.e: After Shankaravarman the dynasty was dominated by the palace guards known as the Tantrins and by rival factions. In 939 [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] chose [[e:yashaskara|Yashaskara]] as king, and the throne later passed to the [[s:parvagupta-dynasty|Parvagupta dynasty]].

unelli.t: Gallic people of the Cotentin peninsula whose leader Viridovix headed a coalition against Caesar in 56 BCE.
unelli.o: The Unelli held the Cotentin in western [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]]. Caesar lists them among the Armorican peoples who submitted to [[e:publius-licinius-crassus|Publius Crassus]] in 57 BCE.
unelli.r: In 56 BCE their chief [[e:viridovix|Viridovix]] commanded a large army of the Unelli, [[s:lexovii|Lexovii]], [[s:aulerci-eburovices|Aulerci Eburovices]] and others, showing how a war leader could unite several peoples.
unelli.e: [[e:quintus-titurius-sabinus|Quintus Titurius Sabinus]] lured the coalition into attacking his fortified camp uphill and routed it, and the Unelli submitted. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town moved from Crociatonum to [[e:coutances|Cosedia]], renamed [[e:salamis-cyprus|Constantia]] in late antiquity, the origin of Coutances and of the name Cotentin.

ubykhia.t: The land of the Ubykhs around Sochi, a small Black Sea people who led the last Circassian resistance and whose language died out in 1992.
ubykhia.o: The Ubykhs lived on the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] coast and mountain valleys around modern [[e:sochi|Sochi]], between the [[s:shapsugs|Shapsugs]] and the [[e:abkhaz-people|Abkhaz]]. They spoke a distinct Northwest Caucasian language with a famously large number of consonants. They are recorded as a separate people by the 17th century; earlier history is little known.
ubykhia.r: Ubykh society was led by noble families, above all the Berzeg, together with free communities, and lived by farming, herding and sea trade with Ottoman ports. In 1861 the Ubykhs hosted the Circassian assembly at [[e:sochi|Sochi]], led by [[e:haji-kerantukh-berzeg|Haji Kerantukh Berzeg]], which appealed to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] for help against [[e:russia|Russia]].
ubykhia.e: The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] overran Ubykhia in 1864, and the entire Ubykh people were expelled to the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]]. Their language faded in exile; its last fluent speaker, [[e:tevfik-esenc|Tevfik Esenc]], died in [[e:turkey|Turkey]] in 1992.

ural-cossack-host.t: A self-governing Cossack community on the Ural River, guardians of Russia's steppe frontier and the starting point of Pugachev's great rebellion.
ural-cossack-host.o: [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]], many from the [[e:don-river|Don]], settled on the [[e:ural-river|Yaik]] River, later renamed the Ural, in the late 16th century, establishing a fishing and raiding community. In 1591 they took part in a Russian campaign, and the host is traditionally dated to that year. Their main town, [[e:oral-kazakhstan|Yaitsky Gorodok]], later became Uralsk.
ural-cossack-host.r: The host was governed by an elected ataman and an assembly, the krug, and lived by fishing for sturgeon and caviar on the river, held in common, and by military service. Many were [[e:old-believers|Old Believers]]. As the Russian state tightened control, discontent grew; in 1772 a revolt broke out, and in 1773 [[e:ural-river|Yaik]] [[e:cossacks|Cossacks]] backed [[e:yemelyan-pugachev|Yemelyan Pugachev's]] rebellion against [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine the Great]].
ural-cossack-host.e: After the revolt, [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine]] renamed the [[e:ural-river|Yaik]] the Ural and the host the Ural [[e:cossacks|Cossack]] Host. It served [[e:russia|Russia]] in Central Asian campaigns. During the [[e:russian-civil-war|Russian Civil War]] the Ural Cossacks fought the Bolsheviks, and the host was destroyed in 1920.

upper-palatinate.t: The Wittelsbach iron country north of the Danube, ruled from Amberg for the Electors Palatine until Bavaria seized it in the Thirty Years' War.
upper-palatinate.o: By the Treaty of [[s:commune-of-pavia|Pavia]] in 1329, [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Louis the Bavarian]] divided the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] possessions, giving the [[e:rhineland|Rhineland]] [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] and the northern part of the [[e:nordgau|Bavarian Nordgau]] to his nephews. This upland region between [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] and the Bohemian border, ruled from [[e:amberg|Amberg]], became known as the Upper Palatinate, an outlying part of the Electoral Palatinate.
upper-palatinate.r: A governor in [[e:amberg|Amberg]] ran the land for the [[e:prince-elector|electors]] in [[e:heidelberg|Heidelberg]]; from 1595 this was Christian of [[s:principality-of-anhalt|Anhalt]], architect of Protestant policy. The region's wealth came from iron mining and smelting around Amberg and [[e:sulzbach-rosenberg|Sulzbach]], which made it the [[e:ruhr|Ruhr]] of the [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]]. Its people were obliged to follow their rulers through [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] and [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]], often against the wishes of the estates.
upper-palatinate.e: After Elector [[e:frederick-v-of-the-palatinate|Frederick V]]'s defeat at the [[e:battle-of-white-mountain|White Mountain]] in 1620, [[e:maximilian-i-elector-of-bavaria|Duke Maximilian]] I of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] occupied the Upper [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]] and in 1628 annexed it, re-Catholicising the population. The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] confirmed it as part of the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]].

united-kingdom.t: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the state that emerged from Irish partition in 1922 and has remained a leading European power.
united-kingdom.o: When the [[s:irish-free-state|Irish Free State]] left in December 1922, the remaining state continued as the [[s:united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-ireland|United Kingdom]], formally renamed the United [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Kingdom of Great Britain]] and [[s:northern-ireland|Northern Ireland]] in 1927. It still ruled a large empire and was a major power after the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]].
united-kingdom.r: The UK is a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]] with a Parliament at [[e:palace-of-westminster|Westminster]], uncodified constitution and [[e:common-law|common law]] in [[e:england|England]] and [[e:wales|Wales]], with separate Scots law. It fought the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] under [[e:winston-churchill|Churchill]], created the National Health Service and welfare state after 1945, and decolonised its empire. Devolution in 1999 created parliaments or assemblies in [[e:scotland|Scotland]], Wales and [[s:northern-ireland|Northern Ireland]].
united-kingdom.e: The UK joined the [[e:european-economic-community|European Economic Community]] in 1973 and left the [[e:european-union|European Union]] in 2020 after the 2016 referendum. It remains a permanent member of the [[e:united-nations-security-council|UN Security Council]] and a nuclear power.
united-kingdom.re: Christianity; Church of England, Church of Scotland

utigurs.t: A Bulgar nomad people east of the Sea of Azov whom Justinian set against their kinsmen the Kutrigurs in the 6th century.
utigurs.o: The Utigurs appear in Byzantine sources in the early 6th century as one of the two main [[e:bulgars|Bulgar]] or Hunnic groups of the Pontic steppe, living east of the [[e:don-river|Don]] and around the [[e:sea-of-azov|Sea of Azov]], with the related [[s:kutrigurs|Kutrigurs]] to the west. [[e:procopius|Procopius]] traces both to two brothers, sons of a Hunnic king.
utigurs.r: They were pastoral nomads led by chiefs, and [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] paid them [[e:subsidy|subsidies]] to keep them as allies. In 551 and again after the [[e:kutrigurs|Kutrigur]] raid on [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 559, Justinian persuaded their ruler [[e:sandilch|Sandilch]] to attack the [[s:kutrigurs|Kutrigurs]], and the two peoples wore each other down in prolonged warfare.
utigurs.e: The [[e:avars|Avars]] and then the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]] subdued the Utigurs, who were under Turkic rule by 576. They later joined [[e:kubrat|Kubrat's]] [[s:old-great-bulgaria|Old Great Bulgaria]] together with the [[s:onogurs|Onogurs]] and [[s:kutrigurs|Kutrigurs]], before the [[e:khazar-khaganate|Khazars]] absorbed the region.

united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.t: The state formed by uniting Great Britain and Ireland in 1801, centre of the largest empire in history and of the industrial world.
united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.o: After the 1798 rebellion in Ireland, the Acts of Union of 1800, passed by both Parliaments, abolished the [[e:parliament-of-ireland|Irish Parliament]] and merged the [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Kingdom of Great Britain]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-ireland|Kingdom of Ireland]] into one state from 1 January 1801, with Irish members sitting at [[e:palace-of-westminster|Westminster]].
united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.r: The [[s:united-kingdom|United Kingdom]] defeated [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], led the [[e:industrial-revolution|Industrial Revolution]] and built a global empire. Parliamentary reform from 1832, Catholic Emancipation in 1829 and [[e:queen-victoria|Queen Victoria's]] long reign shaped the century. The Great Famine of 1845 to 1852 killed about a million in Ireland and caused mass emigration, and Irish Home Rule became a central political issue.
united-kingdom-of-great-britain-and-irel.e: After the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], the [[e:easter-rising|Easter Rising]] and the [[e:irish-war-of-independence|Irish War of Independence]], the [[e:anglo-irish-treaty|Anglo-Irish Treaty]] of 1921 created the [[s:irish-free-state|Irish Free State]] in 1922. The rest became the [[s:united-kingdom|United Kingdom]], renamed in 1927.

united-states-civil-administration-of-th.t: The American administration of Okinawa and the Ryukyu Islands after the Second World War, which kept them as a military base until their return to Japan in 1972.
united-states-civil-administration-of-th.o: American forces took [[e:okinawa-island|Okinawa]] in 1945 in one of the bloodiest battles of the [[e:pacific-war|Pacific War]] and set up a military government. In 1950 it was replaced by the [[e:united-states|United States]] Civil Administration of the [[e:ryukyu-islands|Ryukyu Islands]], and the [[e:san-francisco|San Francisco]] treaty of 1951 left the islands under American control.
united-states-civil-administration-of-th.r: Final authority lay with American officers, from 1957 a High Commissioner, while a local Government of the [[e:ryukyu-islands|Ryukyu Islands]], created in 1952, handled daily affairs. The military seized farmland for bases, provoking mass protests in the 1950s. The US dollar became the currency in 1958. A reversion movement grew, and in 1968 [[e:ryukyuans|Okinawans]] elected their chief executive, [[e:yara-chobyo|Yara Chobyo]], for the first time.
united-states-civil-administration-of-th.e: The Amami Islands were returned in 1953. Anger erupted in the [[e:koza-riot|Koza riot]] of 1970, and under the [[e:okinawa-reversion-agreement|Okinawa Reversion Agreement]] the remaining islands returned to [[e:japan|Japan]] on 15 May 1972, though major American bases remained.

uganda-protectorate.t: The British protectorate built around the Kingdom of Buganda, which kept African kingdoms and farmers at its heart and became independent Uganda in 1962.
uganda-protectorate.o: After the [[s:imperial-british-east-africa-company|Imperial British East Africa Company]] withdrew, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] declared a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] over [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]] in 1894 and extended it to [[s:kingdom-of-bunyoro|Bunyoro]], Toro, [[s:kingdom-of-ankole|Ankole]] and [[s:busoga-principalities|Busoga]] in the following years, after defeating [[e:kabalega|Kabalega]] of Bunyoro. The [[e:buganda-agreement|Buganda Agreement]] of 1900, negotiated by [[e:harry-johnston|Harry Johnston]], set the terms of British rule and Buganda's privileged place.
uganda-protectorate.r: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] ruled indirectly, using [[e:baganda|Ganda]] chiefs as agents across the [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] and preserving the kingdoms. The [[e:uganda-railway|Uganda Railway]] reached [[e:lake-victoria|Lake Victoria]] in 1901, and African smallholders grew [[e:cotton|cotton]] and later [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], with Indian traders handling much of the commerce. Christian missions spread rapidly. The exile of [[e:mutesa-ii-of-buganda|Kabaka Mutesa II]] from 1953 to 1955 sparked a major crisis.
uganda-protectorate.e: [[s:uganda|Uganda]] became independent on 9 October 1962 under Prime Minister [[e:milton-obote|Milton Obote]], with the kingdoms federated within it, and in 1963 [[e:mutesa-ii-of-buganda|Mutesa II]] became president. Tensions between the central state and [[s:kingdom-of-buganda|Buganda]] shaped its early politics.

unitarian-league.t: An alliance of nine Argentine interior provinces under General José María Paz, defeated by the federalists in 1831.
unitarian-league.o: During the civil wars between [[e:unitarian-party|Unitarians]], who wanted a centralised [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]], and Federalists, General [[e:jose-maria-paz|José María Paz]] took control of [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in 1829. He defeated the federal caudillo [[e:juan-facundo-quiroga|Juan Facundo Quiroga]] at [[e:battle-of-la-tablada|La Tablada]] in 1829 and [[e:battle-of-oncativo|Oncativo]] in 1830, and in 1830 the interior provinces formed the League of the Interior with Paz as Supreme Military Chief.
unitarian-league.r: The league joined nine provinces, including [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]], Tucumán, [[e:salta|Salta]], [[e:mendoza-argentina|Mendoza]] and [[e:san-juan-province-argentina|San Juan]], under Unitarian governors installed with [[e:jose-maria-paz|Paz]]'s backing. It was mainly a military alliance. In response, [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]], [[e:santa-fe-argentina|Santa Fe]] and [[e:entre-rios-province|Entre Ríos]] signed the [[e:federal-pact|Federal Pact]] in January 1831.
unitarian-league.e: In May 1831 [[e:jose-maria-paz|Paz]] was captured when soldiers of [[e:estanislao-lopez|Estanislao López]] brought down his horse with boleadoras. [[e:juan-facundo-quiroga|Quiroga]] defeated the [[e:unitarian-party|Unitarians]] at [[e:battle-of-la-ciudadela|La Ciudadela]] near Tucumán in November 1831, and the provinces joined the [[e:federal-pact|Federal Pact]], forming the [[s:argentine-confederation|Argentine Confederation]].

united-states-military-government-in-cub.t: American military rule over Cuba after the Spanish-American War, which ended yellow fever in Havana and left the island bound by the Platt Amendment.
united-states-military-government-in-cub.o: The [[s:united-states|United States]] entered the Cuban War of Independence in April 1898, destroyed the Spanish fleet off [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] de [[e:cuba|Cuba]] in July and forced [[e:spain|Spain]] to give up Cuba in the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1898|Treaty of Paris]]. On 1 January 1899 Spain formally handed over the island to an American military government, excluding the [[s:republic-of-cuba-in-arms|Republic of Cuba in Arms]].
united-states-military-government-in-cub.r: The military governors, [[e:john-r-brooke|John R. Brooke]] and then [[e:leonard-wood|Leonard Wood]], ruled by decree. They disbanded the Cuban army, built roads, schools and sewers, and organised elections. [[e:walter-reed|Walter Reed's]] commission confirmed [[e:carlos-finlay|Carlos Finlay's]] theory that mosquitoes carried yellow fever, and the disease was eradicated from [[e:havana|Havana]]. American investors bought [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] land and railways. A Cuban convention drafted a constitution in 1900 to 1901.
united-states-military-government-in-cub.e: The convention was forced to adopt the [[e:platt-amendment|Platt Amendment]], which gave the [[s:united-states|United States]] a right to intervene and a naval base at [[e:guantanamo-bay-naval-base|Guantánamo]]. Power passed to President [[e:tomas-estrada-palma|Tomás Estrada Palma]] on 20 May 1902, creating the [[s:republic-of-cuba-1902-1959|Republic of Cuba]] (1902-1959).

ukrainian-peoples-republic-of-soviets.t: The first Soviet government in Ukraine, set up by Bolsheviks in Kharkiv as a rival to the Central Rada in Kiev.
ukrainian-peoples-republic-of-soviets.o: In December 1917, after Bolshevik delegates walked out of a congress of soviets in [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] dominated by supporters of the [[e:central-rada|Central Rada]], they held their own congress in [[e:kharkiv|Kharkiv]]. It proclaimed [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]] a republic of soviets in federation with [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]], in opposition to the [[s:ukrainian-peoples-republic|Ukrainian People's Republic]].
ukrainian-peoples-republic-of-soviets.r: The government, called the [[e:peoples-secretariat|People's Secretariat]], included [[e:yevgenia-bosch|Yevhenia Bosh]], [[e:mykola-skrypnyk|Mykola Skrypnyk]] and [[e:volodymyr-zatonsky|Volodymyr Zatonsky]]. It depended heavily on [[e:red-guards-russia|Red Guards]] sent from [[e:russia|Russia]], which under [[e:mikhail-artemyevich-muravyov|Mikhail Muravyov]] captured [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] in February 1918 and carried out mass killings there. Its authority was weak, and several other Soviet republics existed alongside it in eastern and southern [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]].
ukrainian-peoples-republic-of-soviets.e: After the [[e:treaty-of-brest-litovsk|Treaty of Brest-Litovsk]], German and Austro-Hungarian troops drove the Bolsheviks out of [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]]. In March 1918 the republic merged with the other Soviet republics into the [[e:ukrainian-soviet-republic|Ukrainian Soviet Republic]], which was dissolved in April as its leaders withdrew to [[e:russia|Russia]].

uzbek-ssr.t: The Soviet republic of the Uzbeks, Central Asia's most populous, whose cotton monoculture shaped its economy and drained the Aral Sea.
uzbek-ssr.o: The [[e:uzbeks|Uzbek]] SSR was formed in October 1924 in the national delimitation of Soviet [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]], from parts of the [[s:turkestan-assr|Turkestan ASSR]] and the Bukharan and [[e:khwarazm|Khorezm]] republics. Its first capital was [[e:samarkand|Samarkand]]; [[e:tashkent|Tashkent]] became the capital in 1930. The [[s:tajik-assr|Tajik ASSR]] was part of it until 1929, and [[s:karakalpakstan|Karakalpakstan]] joined in 1936.
uzbek-ssr.r: The republic was transformed by collectivisation, the [[e:latin|Latin]] and then Cyrillic scripts, the hujum campaign against veiling, and purges that killed leaders like [[e:fayzulla-khodzhayev|Fayzulla Khodzhayev]] and [[e:akmal-ikramov|Akmal Ikramov]]. [[e:cotton|Cotton]] became the central crop, irrigated from the [[e:oxus|Amu Darya]] and [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]], causing the [[e:aral-sea|Aral Sea]] to shrink. Under [[e:sharof-rashidov|Sharof Rashidov]], first secretary from 1959 to 1983, the 'cotton scandal' exposed massive fraud. [[e:tashkent|Tashkent]] was rebuilt after the earthquake of 1966.
uzbek-ssr.e: As the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] collapsed, [[e:islam-karimov|Islam Karimov's]] government declared independence on 31 August 1991, and the republic became [[s:uzbekistan|Uzbekistan]].

uzbek-khanate.t: The nomadic khanate of Abu'l-Khayr Khan on the Kazakh steppe, from which both the Uzbek dynasties of Transoxiana and the Kazakhs emerged.
uzbek-khanate.o: In 1428 the [[e:shaybanids|Shibanid]] prince [[e:abul-khayr-khan|Abu'l-Khayr]] was proclaimed khan in western [[e:siberia|Siberia]] by the tribes of the former [[s:ulus-of-shiban|Ulus of Shiban]] and [[s:white-horde|White Horde]]. He conquered the steppe as far as the [[e:syr-darya|Syr Darya]] and in 1446 took [[e:sighnaq|Sighnaq]] and other Syr Darya towns, making them his base.
uzbek-khanate.r: [[e:abul-khayr-khan|Abu'l-Khayr]] ruled a confederation of Turkic tribes, including the [[e:qungrat|Qungrat]], [[e:manghud|Mangit]] and Kiyat, known collectively as [[e:uzbeks|Uzbeks]]. He intervened in [[e:timurid-empire|Timurid]] politics, sacking [[e:gurganj|Urgench]] in 1431 and backing the [[e:abu-said-mirza|Timurid Abu Sa'id]]. In 1457 his army was badly defeated by the [[e:oirats|Oirats]], and discontented clans under [[e:kerei-khan|Kerei]] and [[e:janibek-khan|Janibek]] broke away to form the [[s:kazakh-khanate|Kazakh Khanate]].
uzbek-khanate.e: [[e:abul-khayr-khan|Abu'l-Khayr]] died in 1468 and his state collapsed amid rival claims, its tribes passing largely to the [[e:kazakhs|Kazakhs]]. His grandson [[e:muhammad-shaybani|Muhammad Shaybani]] regrouped the [[e:uzbeks|Uzbeks]] and in 1500 conquered [[e:transoxiana|Transoxiana]], founding the [[s:khanate-of-bukhara|Khanate of Bukhara]].

united-states-military-government-of-the.t: American army rule of the Philippines after the Spanish-American War, the regime that fought the Philippine-American War.
united-states-military-government-of-the.o: [[s:united-states|United States]] forces captured [[e:manila|Manila]] from [[e:spain|Spain]] on 13 August 1898, excluding Filipino revolutionaries from the city. Under the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1898|Treaty of Paris]] of December 1898 Spain ceded the islands for 20 million dollars, and President [[e:william-mckinley|William McKinley]] proclaimed a policy of Benevolent Assimilation, governing through a military governor.
united-states-military-government-of-the.r: Military governors, [[e:wesley-merritt|Wesley Merritt]], [[e:elwell-otis|Elwell Otis]], [[e:arthur-macarthur-jr|Arthur MacArthur]] and [[e:adna-chaffee|Adna Chaffee]], held executive and legislative power. From February 1899 the army fought the [[s:first-philippine-republic|First Philippine Republic]] in a brutal war marked by village burnings, reconcentration camps and heavy civilian deaths from disease and famine. At the same time it set up municipal governments, schools and courts.
united-states-military-government-of-the.e: A civilian [[s:insular-government-of-the-philippine-islands|Insular Government of the Philippine Islands]] under [[e:william-howard-taft|William Howard Taft]] took over most functions in July 1901. On 4 July 1902 the war was declared over and military government formally ended, though fighting continued in places, especially in [[e:moro-people|Moro]] areas.

ur.t: A rich Sumerian port city of the moon god Nanna, famous for the treasures of its Royal Cemetery and the First Dynasty of Ur.
ur.o: Ur lay near the mouth of the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]], close to the shore of the Gulf, and was settled from the [[e:ubaid-period|Ubaid period]]. In the Early Dynastic III period, around 2600 BCE, it emerged as one of the leading Sumerian cities, and the [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] records a [[e:old-babylonian-empire|First Dynasty]] of Ur founded by [[e:mesannepadda|Mesannepadda]].
ur.r: Ur prospered on trade by sea with [[s:dilmun|Dilmun]], [[s:magan|Magan]] and [[e:meluhha|Meluhha]], bringing [[e:copper|copper]], carnelian and lapis lazuli into [[e:sumer|Sumer]]. [[e:leonard-woolley|Leonard Woolley's]] excavations of 1922 to 1934 uncovered the Royal Cemetery, with the gold helmet of [[e:meskalamdug|Meskalamdug]], the tomb of Queen [[e:puabi|Puabi]], the [[e:standard-of-ur|Standard of Ur]] and lyres, alongside evidence of attendants buried with their masters. The city's patron was [[e:nanna|Nanna]], the moon god.
ur.e: Ur fell under [[e:lugal-zage-si|Lugal-zage-si]] and then the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]]. After [[s:gutian-rule|Gutian rule]], [[e:ur-nammu|Ur-Nammu]] founded a [[e:third-dynasty-of-ur|Third Dynasty]] in 2112 BCE and made Ur the capital of the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]], building its great [[e:ziggurat|ziggurat]]. The city remained inhabited until about the 4th century BCE, when the river shifted away.

uwajima-domain.t: A Date family domain in southwestern Shikoku whose reforming lord Date Munenari built one of Japan's first steamships.
uwajima-domain.o: In 1614 the [[e:shogun|shogunate]] granted [[e:uwajima|Uwajima]] in [[e:iyo-province|Iyo]] province, with 100,000 koku, to [[e:date-hidemune|Date Hidemune]], the eldest son of [[e:date-masamune|Date Masamune]], who had been passed over as heir to the [[s:sendai-domain|Sendai Domain]]. Hidemune entered Uwajima castle in 1615.
uwajima-domain.r: [[e:date-hidemune|Hidemune]]'s descendants ruled until 1871 as an independent branch of the Date. The domain lived from [[e:rice|rice]], fisheries and paper on a rugged coast. In the 1850s [[e:date-munenari|Date Munenari]], counted among the four wise lords of the late [[e:shogun|shogunate]], sheltered the Western scholar [[e:takano-choei|Takano Choei]], hired [[e:omura-masujiro|Murata Zoroku]], later Omura Masujiro, and had a working steamship built with local craftsmen.
uwajima-domain.e: [[e:date-munenari|Munenari]] took part in the councils that shaped the new government in 1868, and served in early Meiji diplomacy. After abolition in 1871 the domain became part of [[e:ehime-prefecture|Ehime Prefecture]].

ui-fidgenti.t: Kingdom of west County Limerick whose king Donnubán sided with the Vikings of Limerick against Brian Bóruma, and from whom the O'Donovans descend.
ui-fidgenti.o: The Uí Fidgenti claimed descent from Fiachu Fidgenid, a kinsman of the [[e:eoganachta|Eóganachta]], and held much of what is now [[e:county-limerick|County Limerick]] west of the [[e:river-maigue|Maigue]] from the early [[e:middle-ages|medieval period]]. They formed a subject but partly privileged kingdom within the [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Kingdom of Munster]], divided into branches such as the [[e:ui-chonaill-gabra|Uí Chonaill Gabra]].
ui-fidgenti.r: The kingdom rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] and the fertile lands south of the [[e:river-shannon|Shannon]]. In the 10th century it was caught between the rising [[e:dal-cais|Dál Cais of Thomond]] and the Norse town of [[e:limerick|Limerick]]. Its king [[e:donnuban-mac-cathail|Donnubán mac Cathail]] allied with [[e:ivar-of-limerick|Ivar of Limerick]] and helped bring about the death of [[e:mathgamain-mac-cennetig|Mathgamain]], brother of [[e:brian-boru|Brian Bóruma]], in 976, which drew Brian's revenge.
ui-fidgenti.e: After Brian's victories the Uí Fidgenti were reduced, and in the late 12th century the [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] advance into [[e:limerick|Limerick]], especially by the [[e:fitzgerald-dynasty|FitzGeralds]], displaced them. [[e:donnuban-mac-cathail|Donnubán]]'s descendants, the [[e:odonovan-family|O'Donovans]], moved south into [[e:county-cork|Cork]], where they held lordships near [[e:skibbereen|Skibbereen]] for centuries.

united-kingdom-of-israel.t: The United Monarchy of Saul, David and Solomon, remembered in the Bible as Israel's golden age, whose scale historians still debate.
united-kingdom-of-israel.o: According to the [[e:hebrew-bible|Hebrew Bible]], the Israelite tribes, pressed by the [[s:philistine-pentapolis|Philistine Pentapolis]], made [[e:saul|Saul]] their king in the late 11th century BCE. [[e:david|David]] then united [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Israel]] and [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]], captured [[s:urusalim|Urusalim]] and made [[e:jerusalem|Jerusalem]] his capital.
united-kingdom-of-israel.r: The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] describes [[e:david|David's]] conquests of [[s:moab|Moab]], [[s:ammon|Ammon]], [[s:edom|Edom]] and [[s:aram-zobah|Aram-Zobah]], and [[e:solomon|Solomon's]] temple, palace and trade with [[e:hiram-i|Hiram I]] of [[s:tyre|Tyre]]. Archaeology confirms a dynasty called the [[e:house-of-david|House of David]] in the 9th-century [[e:tel-dan-stele|Tel Dan stele]], but the size and wealth of the kingdom are much debated. [[e:yhwh|Yahweh]] was the national god.
united-kingdom-of-israel.e: After [[e:solomon|Solomon's]] death c. 930 BCE, the northern tribes rejected his son [[e:rehoboam|Rehoboam]] and made [[e:jeroboam-i|Jeroboam]] king, splitting the realm into the [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Kingdom of Israel]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Kingdom of Judah]]. The memory of the united monarchy shaped Jewish and later messianic hopes.

united-states-virgin-islands.t: The former Danish West Indies, bought by the United States in 1917 to guard the Panama Canal approaches and now an unincorporated US territory.
united-states-virgin-islands.o: Fearing that [[e:germany|Germany]] might acquire a base in the [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] during the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], the [[s:united-states|United States]] bought [[e:saint-thomas-u-s-virgin-islands|Saint Thomas]], [[e:saint-john-u-s-virgin-islands|Saint John]] and [[e:saint-croix|Saint Croix]] from [[e:denmark|Denmark]] for 25 million dollars in gold. The [[s:danish-west-indies|Danish West Indies]] were handed over on 31 March 1917, now celebrated as Transfer Day.
united-states-virgin-islands.r: Until 1931 the islands were run by the [[e:united-states-navy|US Navy]], with naval officers as governors, and the inhabitants became US citizens only in 1927. [[e:organic-acts-of-the-virgin-islands|Organic Acts]] of 1936 and 1954 created a local legislature, and [[e:melvin-evans|Melvin Evans]] became the first elected governor in 1970. The decline of [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]] and the end of [[e:prohibition-in-the-united-states|Prohibition]] hurt the economy, which later turned to tourism, cruise shipping and, on [[e:saint-croix|Saint Croix]], a large oil refinery that closed in 2012.
united-states-virgin-islands.e: The islands remain an unincorporated, organised territory with a non-voting delegate in Congress. [[e:hurricane-irma|Hurricanes Irma]] and Maria struck in 2017, and the territory continues to debate its status and its Danish and African heritage.
