uaxactun.t: A Maya city in the Petén just north of Tikal, home to one of the first excavated Maya astronomical complexes and long overshadowed by its larger neighbour.
uaxactun.o: Uaxactun was settled in the Middle Preclassic and developed monumental architecture by about 300 BCE. Its [[e:late-preclassic|Late Preclassic]] pyramid E-VII-sub, decorated with large stucco masks, belongs to an 'E Group', a plaza arrangement once interpreted as aligned to solstice and equinox sunrises.
uaxactun.r: Uaxactun was ruled by its own lords, but its history is entwined with [[s:tikal|Tikal]], about 20 kilometres to the south. Inscriptions record the arrival of the Teotihuacan-linked lord [[e:siyaj-kak|Sihyaj K'ahk']] in 378 CE, after which Uaxactun appears under Tikal's influence. Its Early Classic murals and palace sequence were studied in detail by the [[e:carnegie-institution-for-science|Carnegie Institution]] in the 1920s and 1930s.
uaxactun.e: Monument building ended around 900 CE, during the wider [[e:classic-maya-collapse|Classic Maya collapse]], and the city was abandoned. Its excavation produced a ceramic sequence that long served as the basis for dating the Maya lowlands.

upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom.t: A small tribal sheikhdom of the Aulaqi people, separate from the neighbouring Aulaqi sultanates, in the hinterland of British Aden.
upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom.o: The Aulaqi tribes of the [[e:shabwa|Shabwa]] region were divided among several rulers. The Upper Aulaqi Sheikhdom, with its seat at Said, emerged as a distinct polity by around 1800, alongside the [[s:upper-aulaqi-sultanate|Upper Aulaqi Sultanate]] and the [[s:lower-aulaqi-sultanate|Lower Aulaqi Sultanate]].
upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom.r: Its sheikhs ruled by tribal custom over a mountainous and semi-desert district. Like its neighbours it signed protection treaties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and became part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. In 1959 it was one of the six founding members of the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]]. Little else is recorded of its internal history.
upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom.e: In 1967 the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over the region and the sheikhdom was abolished and incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

uyghur-khaganate.t: A Turkic steppe empire that made Manichaeism its state religion, built cities in Mongolia and rescued the Tang dynasty during the An Lushan rebellion.
uyghur-khaganate.o: The [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]], a leading tribe of the Toquz Oghuz confederation, joined the [[e:basmyls|Basmyls]] and [[s:karluk-yabgu|Karluks]] to overthrow the [[s:second-turkic-khaganate|Second Turkic Khaganate]] in 744. Their chief [[e:qutlugh-bilge-kol-qaghan|Qutlugh Bilge Kol Qaghan]] then turned on his allies, becoming master of the Mongolian steppe.
uyghur-khaganate.r: [[e:bayanchur-khan|Bayanchur Khan]] built the walled capital [[e:ordu-baliq|Ordu-Baliq]] on the [[e:orkhon-river|Orkhon River]]. The [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]] helped the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] recover [[e:changan|Chang'an]] and [[e:luoyang|Luoyang]] from [[e:an-lushan|An Lushan's]] rebels in 757, and won a lucrative trade of horses for [[e:silk|silk]]. In 762 [[e:bogu-qaghan|Bogu Qaghan]] adopted [[e:manichaeism|Manichaeism]] from Sogdian missionaries, making the Uyghurs the only state to adopt it officially. Sogdian scribes and merchants were influential at court.
uyghur-khaganate.e: Weakened by famine, epidemic and succession disputes, the khaganate fell in 840 when the [[s:yenisei-kyrgyz-khaganate|Yenisei Kyrgyz Khaganate]] sacked [[e:ordu-baliq|Ordu-Baliq]]. [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] groups fled south-west, founding the [[s:kingdom-of-qocho|Kingdom of Qocho]] and the Ganzhou Uyghur state, and later formed part of the [[s:kara-khanid-khanate|Kara-Khanid Khanate]].

united-suvadive-republic.t: A breakaway state of the southern Maldive atolls that rebelled against Male's control between 1959 and 1963.
united-suvadive-republic.o: Discontent in the three southernmost atolls, [[e:addu-atoll|Addu]], [[e:huvadhu-atoll|Huvadhu]] and [[e:fuvahmulah|Fuvahmulah]], over taxes and Male's attempts to restrict trade led to revolt in 1959. [[e:abdullah-afeef|Abdullah Afeef]], a local leader at Addu, where the British had an air base at [[e:gan-addu-atoll|Gan]], was declared president of the United Suvadive Republic, with [[e:hithadhoo|Hithadhoo]] as its capital.
united-suvadive-republic.r: The republic traded directly with [[e:ceylon|Ceylon]] and with the British base, and set up its own government and postal system. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] offered tacit support but never granted recognition. The government in Male under prime minister [[e:ibrahim-nasir|Ibrahim Nasir]] sent armed forces, which suppressed the [[e:huvadhu-atoll|Huvadhu]] rebels in 1962.
united-suvadive-republic.e: The republic was dissolved in 1963, and [[e:abdullah-afeef|Afeef]] went into exile in the [[s:british-seychelles|Seychelles]] with British help. The atolls returned to the [[s:sultanate-of-the-maldives|Sultanate of the Maldives]].

united-provinces-of-new-granada.t: A federation of New Granada's provinces during the 'Foolish Fatherland', torn by civil war before the Spanish reconquest of 1816.
united-provinces-of-new-granada.o: After the revolutions of 1810, delegates of several provinces of the [[s:viceroyalty-of-new-granada|Viceroyalty of New Granada]] signed an [[e:act-of-federation-of-the-united-provinces-of-new-granada|Act of Federation]] in November 1811, creating the United Provinces of [[e:new-granada|New Granada]]. Its congress sat at [[e:tunja|Tunja]] and was led by [[e:camilo-torres-tenorio|Camilo Torres]]. Cartagena declared absolute independence from [[e:spain|Spain]] the same month.
united-provinces-of-new-granada.r: The federation left great power to the provinces and quarrelled with the centralist [[s:free-and-independent-state-of-cundinamarca|Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca]], leading to civil war. [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]], a refugee from [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]], wrote his [[e:cartagena-manifesto|Cartagena Manifesto]] there in 1812 and led campaigns for the federation. In 1814 he captured [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] for the [[s:dutch-republic|United Provinces]], which then moved its government there.
united-provinces-of-new-granada.e: [[e:pablo-morillo|Pablo Morillo's]] royalist expedition besieged Cartagena in 1815, starving it into surrender, and took [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] in May 1816. Leaders such as [[e:camilo-torres-tenorio|Camilo Torres]] and the scientist [[e:francisco-jose-de-caldas|Francisco José de Caldas]] were executed. The period is remembered as the [[e:patria-boba|Patria Boba]], the Foolish Fatherland.

uqaylid-dynasty.t: A Bedouin Arab dynasty that ruled Mosul and the Jazira for a century between the Buyids and the Seljuks, at times reaching Aleppo.
uqaylid-dynasty.o: The Banu Uqayl were an Arab tribe of the [[e:upper-mesopotamia|Jazira]] who served the [[s:hamdanid-emirate-of-mosul|Hamdanid emirate of Mosul]]. Around 990, as [[e:hamdanid-dynasty|Hamdanid]] and [[e:buyid-dynasty|Buyid]] power waned, the Uqaylid chief Muhammad ibn al-Musayyab took [[e:mosul|Mosul]], and his family went on to rule northern [[e:iraq|Iraq]] and parts of the upper [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]].
uqaylid-dynasty.r: The Uqaylids ruled as tribal [[e:emir|emirs]], relying on [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] cavalry and taxing the farmlands and trade of the [[e:upper-mesopotamia|Jazira]]. They were Shia. [[e:qirwash-ibn-al-muqallad|Qirwash ibn al-Muqallad]], who reigned for about half a century from 1001, briefly recognised the [[s:fatimid-caliphate|Fatimid Caliphate]] in 1010 before returning to the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]]. [[e:muslim-ibn-quraysh|Muslim ibn Quraysh]], called Sharaf al-Dawla, extended Uqaylid rule to [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]] in 1080, making the dynasty a major power in [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
uqaylid-dynasty.e: [[e:muslim-ibn-quraysh|Muslim ibn Quraysh]] was killed in 1085 fighting [[e:suleiman-ibn-qutalmish|Sulayman ibn Qutalmish]] of the [[s:sultanate-of-rum|Sultanate of Rum]]. The [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] took [[e:mosul|Mosul]] in 1096, and Uqaylid branches lingered only in a few fortresses such as [[e:qalat-jabar|Qal'at Ja'bar]].

upper-aulaqi-sultanate.t: A sultanate of the Aulaqi tribes based at Nisab, one of the protected states in the hinterland of British Aden.
upper-aulaqi-sultanate.o: The Aulaqi tribes of the [[e:shabwa|Shabwa]] region formed several states. The Upper Aulaqi Sultanate, based at Nisab, emerged as a distinct power by around 1800, alongside the [[s:upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom|Upper Aulaqi Sheikhdom]] and the [[s:lower-aulaqi-sultanate|Lower Aulaqi Sultanate]].
upper-aulaqi-sultanate.r: The sultans ruled a large but thinly populated territory of wadis and highland plateaus, where the Aulaqi were known as formidable fighters, many serving abroad as soldiers. The sultanate entered British protection by treaty and formed part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. It joined the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]] in the 1960s.
upper-aulaqi-sultanate.e: When the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took power in 1967, the sultanate was abolished and incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

usdiae.t: People of south-eastern Ireland known only from Ptolemy's Geography, placed inland near the Brigantes and Coriondi.
usdiae.o: The Usdiae appear in [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 in the south-east of Ireland, inland of the coastal [[s:brigantes-ireland|Brigantes (Ireland)]] and [[s:manapii|Manapii]] and near the [[s:coriondi|Coriondi]], roughly in the region of modern [[e:kilkenny|Kilkenny]], [[e:county-carlow|Carlow]] or [[s:kingdom-of-loigis|Laois]]. As with all of Ptolemy's Irish names, the data came second-hand from earlier sea reports.
usdiae.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers, settlements or way of life, and no convincing link has been found between their name and any people of early Irish tradition. The fertile lands of the [[e:river-barrow|Barrow]] and [[e:river-nore|Nore]] valleys in this region supported mixed farming and [[e:cattle|cattle]]-raising.
usdiae.e: The Usdiae do not appear again in any source. The region where Ptolemy placed them later belonged to the [[s:kingdom-of-osraige|Kingdom of Osraige]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Kingdom of Leinster]].

ukhaydirid-emirate.t: An Alid dynasty that ruled the oases of al-Yamama in central Arabia for nearly two centuries.
ukhaydirid-emirate.o: Around 866 [[e:muhammad-ibn-yusuf-al-ukhaydir|Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Ukhaydir]], a descendant of al-[[e:hasan-ibn-ali|Hasan ibn Ali]], fled the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]] after a failed revolt and took control of al-[[e:yamama|Yamama]] in [[e:najd|Najd]]. He founded a dynasty with its seat at al-Khidrima, in the region of modern [[e:al-kharj|al-Kharj]] south of [[e:riyadh|Riyadh]].
ukhaydirid-emirate.r: The Ukhaydirids governed farming oases and the [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] tribes around them. Later sources describe them as [[e:zaydism|Zaydi Shi'is]]. Their land lay on pilgrimage and trade routes between [[e:iraq|Iraq]], [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] and the [[s:kingdom-of-hejaz|Hejaz]], and the Persian traveller [[e:nasir-khusraw|Nasir Khusraw]], who passed in the 1050s, mentions the fortified seat of its [[e:alids|Alid]] [[e:emir|emirs]].
ukhaydirid-emirate.e: The rise of the [[s:qarmatians-of-bahrain|Qarmatians of Bahrain]] to the east reduced the [[e:emirate|emirate]] to a client. It faded in the mid-11th century, with little recorded about its end, and al-[[e:yamama|Yamama]] fell under local tribal chiefs.

uyunid-emirate.t: An Arab dynasty of the Abd al-Qays tribe that ended Qarmatian rule in eastern Arabia and governed al-Ahsa and Qatif for nearly two centuries.
uyunid-emirate.o: In 1076 [[e:abd-allah-ibn-ali-al-uyuni|Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Uyuni]], a chief of the Abd al-[[e:qays|Qays]] tribe, rebelled against the [[s:qarmatians-of-bahrain|Qarmatians of Bahrain]]. With the help of a [[s:seljuk-empire|Seljuk Empire]] army he took [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Ahsa]] in 1077 and founded an [[e:emirate|emirate]] covering the oases and coast of eastern [[e:arabia|Arabia]] and the [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] islands.
uyunid-emirate.r: Much of what is known comes from the poetry of [[e:ibn-al-muqarrab|Ibn al-Muqarrab]], a member of the family, and its commentary. The [[e:emirate|emirate]] controlled the date groves of [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Ahsa]] and [[e:qatif|Qatif]] and the pearl banks around [[e:bahrain-island|Awal]], the main [[s:sheikhdom-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] island. It was weakened by family quarrels and lost the islands for a time to the [[s:emirate-of-kish|Emirate of Kish]].
uyunid-emirate.e: By the 13th century the Uyunids were reduced to a weak local power. Around 1253 the [[s:usfurid-dynasty|Usfurid dynasty]] of the [[e:banu-amir|Banu Amir]] took [[e:al-ahsa-oasis|al-Ahsa]] and replaced them.

united-belgian-states.t: The first independent Belgian state, a confederation formed in the Brabant Revolution of 1789–1790 and modelled partly on the United States.
united-belgian-states.o: [[e:joseph-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Joseph II]]'s reforms of courts, church and administration angered the estates of the [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]]. In 1789 exiles organised an army at [[e:breda|Breda]], defeated the Austrians at [[e:battle-of-turnhout-1789|Turnhout]] in October, and by December drove them from most of the country. On 11 January 1790 the provinces declared independence as the United Belgian States.
united-belgian-states.r: The confederation's treaty created a sovereign congress in [[e:brussels|Brussels]] while leaving each province its old institutions. Power lay with the conservative Statists of [[e:henri-van-der-noot|Henri van der Noot]], who defended traditional privileges and the Church, against the democratic Vonckists of [[e:jean-francois-vonck|Jean-François Vonck]], who were driven into exile. No foreign power recognised the state.
united-belgian-states.e: Divided and without allies, the United Belgian States collapsed when [[e:leopold-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Leopold II's]] Austrian army reoccupied the country in December 1790. The [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]] was restored until the French conquest of 1794.

uaymil.t: A thinly documented Maya province of south-eastern Yucatán, conquered with great brutality by the Spanish in the 1540s.
uaymil.o: Uaymil emerged after the fall of the [[s:league-of-mayapan|League of Mayapan]] around 1441 in the south-east of the peninsula, between the provinces of [[s:cochuah|Cochuah]] and [[s:chetumal|Chetumal]], in what is now southern [[e:quintana-roo|Quintana Roo]]. Little is known of its origins.
uaymil.r: It appears to have been a loose grouping of towns in a region of lagoons and forest, known only from a few colonial sources. Its people farmed [[e:maize|maize]] and probably [[e:cacao|cacao]] and took part in coastal trade.
uaymil.e: In 1544 the Spanish captains [[e:gaspar-pacheco|Gaspar]] and [[e:melchor-pacheco|Melchor Pacheco]] conquered Uaymil and its neighbours with exceptional cruelty, and the region was largely depopulated. It became part of the [[s:province-of-yucatan|Province of Yucatán]].

upper-yafa-sultanate.t: A loose sultanate of the upper Yafa highlands, one of the most independent of the British protectorate states of south Arabia.
upper-yafa-sultanate.o: Like its neighbour the [[s:lower-yafa-sultanate|Lower Yafa Sultanate]], Upper [[e:yafa|Yafa]] emerged in the early 18th century when the Yafa tribes rejected rule by the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]]. The sultans of the Harhara family, based at Mahjaba, held a loose primacy over the upper Yafa clans and their sheikhdoms.
upper-yafa-sultanate.r: Authority was weak and shared with several sheikhs, and the sultanate had almost no administration. Its rugged highlands were famous for their stone tower houses and terraces, and many of its men emigrated or served as soldiers in [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Hadramawt]] and [[e:india|India]]. Upper [[e:yafa|Yafa]] entered British protection late and stayed outside the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]], remaining part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]].
upper-yafa-sultanate.e: In 1967, as British rule ended, the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took control and Upper [[e:yafa|Yafa]] was incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

umbrians.t: Italic people of central Italy, called by Pliny the oldest in Italy, whose ritual Iguvine Tablets are the longest surviving text in any Italic language other than Latin.
umbrians.o: The Umbrians lived in the upper [[e:tiber-river|Tiber]] valley and the [[e:apennines|Apennines]] east of [[e:etruria|Etruria]] from the early 1st millennium BCE. Ancient writers believed they had once held a much larger area before being pushed back by [[e:etruscans|Etruscans]] and [[e:gaul|Gauls]]. They spoke Umbrian, an [[e:osco-umbrian-languages|Osco-Umbrian]] language.
umbrians.r: Umbrian communities were independent towns and hill sanctuaries, among them [[e:gubbio|Iguvium]], [[e:todi|Tuder]], [[e:assisi|Asisium]], [[e:bevagna|Mevania]], [[e:spoleto|Spoletium]] and [[e:amelia-umbria|Ameria]], without a lasting central government. The [[e:iguvine-tablets|Iguvine Tablets]], seven bronze plates of the 3rd to 1st centuries BCE, set out the rituals of the [[e:atiedian-brethren|Atiedian Brethren]], a priestly college of Iguvium, giving rich detail on Italic religion. [[e:bronze|Bronze]] votive figures from mountain shrines are typical of their art.
umbrians.e: [[e:rome|Rome]] founded [[e:narni|Narnia]] in 299 BCE, and after the [[e:battle-of-sentinum|battle of Sentinum]] in 295 BCE, where some Umbrians backed the anti-Roman coalition, the Umbrian towns became allies. The last resistance, at [[e:sarsina|Sarsina]], ended in 266 BCE. They gained citizenship after the [[e:social-war-91-87-bce|Social War]], and the name survives in the Italian region of [[e:umbria|Umbria]].

unyanyembe.t: The leading Nyamwezi chiefdom of central Tanzania, whose town of Tabora became the main inland hub of the 19th-century caravan trade.
unyanyembe.o: Unyanyembe was one of many Nyamwezi chiefdoms in the plateau of west-central [[s:tanzania|Tanzania]]. From the early 19th century Nyamwezi porters and traders opened [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] to the coast, and in the 1840s Arab and [[e:swahili|Swahili merchants]] settled at [[e:tabora|Tabora]], which grew into a commercial town under the chief Fundikira.
unyanyembe.r: The ntemi (chief) ruled with councils of elders and drew wealth from the [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slave caravans that passed between the coast and the [[e:great-lakes|Great Lakes]]. Relations with the Arab traders were tense: in the 1860s chief Mnywasele was overthrown in a war in which the traders backed his rival. Explorers including [[e:richard-francis-burton|Burton]], [[e:john-hanning-speke|Speke]], [[e:david-livingstone|Livingstone]] and [[e:henry-morton-stanley|Stanley]] stayed at [[e:tabora|Tabora]].
unyanyembe.e: Chief Isike resisted the Germans, and in 1893, when his fortress was stormed, he took his own life. Unyanyembe was absorbed into [[s:german-east-africa|German East Africa]], and [[e:tabora|Tabora]] became a colonial administrative and railway centre.

united-kingdom-of-the-netherlands.t: The kingdom created at the Congress of Vienna to unite the northern and southern Low Countries under William I, broken apart by the Belgian Revolution.
united-kingdom-of-the-netherlands.o: The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] joined the former [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] and the [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]] into one kingdom as a barrier against [[e:france|France]]. William I, sovereign prince of the [[s:sovereign-principality-of-the-united-netherlands|Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands]], proclaimed himself king in March 1815, and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and allied troops fought at [[e:battle-of-waterloo|Waterloo]] that June. He also became grand duke of [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]].
united-kingdom-of-the-netherlands.r: William I ruled energetically, with the capital alternating between [[e:brussels|Brussels]] and [[e:the-hague|The Hague]]. He founded universities at [[e:ghent|Ghent]] and [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]], the [[e:societe-generale-de-belgique|Société Générale]] bank and supported industry such as [[e:john-cockerill|Cockerill]]'s ironworks. But the south, more populous and largely Catholic and French-speaking among its elites, resented Dutch-dominated government, language policy and taxes.
united-kingdom-of-the-netherlands.e: After a riot at a [[e:brussels|Brussels]] opera performance in August 1830, the [[e:belgian-revolution|Belgian Revolution]] drove out [[e:dutch|Dutch]] troops and created the [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Kingdom of Belgium]]. William refused to accept this until the [[e:treaty-of-london-1839|Treaty of London]] in 1839, which left the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]] in the north.

ukrainian-ssr.t: Soviet Ukraine, the Soviet Union's second-largest republic, which suffered the Holodomor and the Second World War and became independent Ukraine in 1991.
ukrainian-ssr.o: After two earlier attempts, Bolshevik forces proclaimed a Ukrainian Socialist Soviet Republic in January 1919, with [[e:kharkiv|Kharkiv]] as capital. Despite defeats by the Whites and [[e:poles|Poles]], the Soviet regime was established by 1920, and in 1922 the republic became a founding member of the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]].
ukrainian-ssr.r: The 1920s brought [[e:ukrainisation|Ukrainisation]] in schools and culture, but [[e:joseph-stalin|Stalin]]'s forced collectivisation caused the famine of 1932 and 1933, the [[e:holodomor|Holodomor]], which killed millions. The capital moved to [[e:kyiv|Kyiv]] in 1934. The republic gained western [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]] in 1939, was devastated by German occupation, joined the [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] in 1945 and received [[e:crimea|Crimea]] in 1954. Leaders such as [[e:petro-shelest|Petro Shelest]] and [[e:volodymyr-shcherbytsky|Volodymyr Shcherbytsky]] ran it for [[e:moscow|Moscow]].
ukrainian-ssr.e: The [[e:chernobyl-disaster|Chernobyl disaster]] in 1986 and the reforms of [[e:mikhail-gorbachev|Gorbachev]] fed a national movement. On 24 August 1991 the [[e:verkhovna-rada|Verkhovna Rada]] declared independence, confirmed by referendum on 1 December, and [[e:leonid-kravchuk|Leonid Kravchuk]] became the first president of independent [[e:ukraine|Ukraine]].

united-arab-emirates.t: A federation of seven emirates formed from the Trucial States in 1971, now a global hub of trade, finance and aviation.
united-arab-emirates.o: After [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] announced its withdrawal from the Gulf, [[e:zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahyan|Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan]] of [[s:sheikhdom-of-abu-dhabi|Abu Dhabi]] and [[e:rashid-bin-saeed-al-maktoum|Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum]] of [[s:sheikhdom-of-dubai|Dubai]] led talks among the [[s:trucial-states|Trucial States]]. On 2 December 1971 six sheikhdoms formed the United Arab [[e:emirate|Emirates]]; the [[s:sheikhdom-of-ras-al-khaimah|Sheikhdom of Ras al-Khaimah]] joined in February 1972. [[s:state-of-bahrain|Bahrain]] and [[s:state-of-qatar|Qatar]] chose separate independence.
united-arab-emirates.r: The Federal Supreme Council of the seven rulers elects the president, traditionally the ruler of [[s:sheikhdom-of-abu-dhabi|Abu Dhabi]], while each [[e:emirate|emirate]] keeps control of its own resources. Abu Dhabi's oil funds the federation, and [[s:sheikhdom-of-dubai|Dubai]] built a trading, tourism and aviation economy around [[e:jebel-ali|Jebel Ali]] port and Emirates airline. Foreign residents make up nearly nine tenths of the population.
united-arab-emirates.e: [[e:zayed-bin-sultan-al-nahyan|Zayed]] was president until his death in 2004, followed by [[e:khalifa|Khalifa]] bin Zayed and in 2022 [[e:mohamed-bin-zayed-al-nahyan|Mohamed bin Zayed]]. The UAE has become an active regional power and normalised relations with [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Israel]] in 2020.

united-states-of-the-ionian-islands.t: British protectorate over the seven Ionian Islands from 1815 to 1864, whose cession to Greece was the first enlargement of the Greek kingdom.
united-states-of-the-ionian-islands.o: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] fall, the [[e:treaty-of-paris-1815|Treaty of Paris]] in November 1815 made the Ionian Islands, formerly the [[s:french-ionian-islands|French Ionian Islands]] and earlier the [[s:septinsular-republic|Septinsular Republic]], a nominally independent state under the exclusive protection of [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]. [[s:corcyra|Corfu]], the last French-held island, had been handed over in 1814.
united-states-of-the-ionian-islands.r: Real power lay with the British Lord High Commissioner. The first, [[e:thomas-maitland|Sir Thomas Maitland]], nicknamed King Tom, imposed the constitution of 1817, which left an island assembly and senate with little authority. The British built roads, [[e:aqueduct|aqueducts]] and the [[e:ionian-academy|Ionian Academy]], but many islanders resented their rule. From the 1840s Radical politicians demanded union with [[e:greece|Greece]], and their assembly voted for it repeatedly.
united-states-of-the-ionian-islands.e: After the [[e:greeks|Greeks]] deposed King Otto, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] agreed to cede the islands to encourage the new [[e:george-i-of-greece|King George I]]. Under the Treaty of London the islands joined the [[s:kingdom-of-greece|Kingdom of Greece]] in 1864, and Corfu's fortifications were partly demolished.

upi.t: Upi, the Late Bronze Age territory of Damascus, the southernmost Syrian land held by Egypt and a frontier with the Hittites.
upi.o: Upi, or Apa, was the oasis of [[e:damascus|Damascus]] and the land around it. It came under the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] after the campaigns of [[e:thutmose-iii|Thutmose III]] in the 15th century BCE, forming one of [[e:egypt|Egypt's]] provinces in [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
upi.r: In the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]], the local ruler [[e:biryawaza|Biryawaza]] acted as [[e:egypt|Egypt's]] agent, defending the area against the [[e:hittite-empire|Hittites]] and their allies such as [[e:aitakkama|Aitakkama]] of [[s:kadesh|Kadesh]]. [[e:damascus|Damascus]] served as a base for Egyptian officials and troops.
upi.e: Upi remained the Egyptian border district after the Battle of Kadesh and the peace treaty of [[e:ramesses-ii|Ramesses II]] and [[e:hattusili-iii|Hattusili III]] c. 1259 BCE. With the collapse of Egyptian power after 1200 BCE, [[e:damascus|Damascus]] later rose again as the capital of [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]].

unfederated-malay-states.t: Collective name for five Malay sultanates under British protection that kept more self-rule than the federated states.
unfederated-malay-states.o: The [[e:anglo-siamese-treaty-of-1909|Anglo-Siamese Treaty of 1909]] transferred Siamese rights over the [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah Sultanate]], [[s:kelantan-sultanate|Kelantan]], [[s:terengganu-sultanate|Terengganu]] and [[s:perlis|Perlis]] to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], which installed British advisers. [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor]], long independent under modernising rulers such as [[e:abu-bakar-of-johor|Abu Bakar]], accepted a general adviser in 1914. These five states, which never joined the [[s:federated-malay-states|Federated Malay States]], were known as the Unfederated Malay States.
unfederated-malay-states.r: There was no common government: each sultan kept his own administration staffed largely by [[e:malays|Malays]], with a British adviser whose advice had to be followed except in religion and custom. [[e:rice|Rice]] farming and fishing dominated the northern states, while [[s:johor-sultanate|Johor]] developed [[e:rubber|rubber]] and pineapple plantations.
unfederated-malay-states.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied them from 1942, handing [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah]], [[s:perlis|Perlis]], [[s:kelantan-sultanate|Kelantan]] and [[s:terengganu-sultanate|Terengganu]] to [[s:thailand|Thailand]] in 1943. In 1946 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] merged them into the [[s:malayan-union|Malayan Union]], replaced in 1948 by the [[s:federation-of-malaya|Federation of Malaya]].

udaipur-state-chhattisgarh.t: A forested feudatory state of northern Chhattisgarh, ruled from Dharamjaigarh by a branch of the house of Sarguja.
udaipur-state-chhattisgarh.o: [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] was a dependency of [[s:surguja-state|Sarguja]] in the [[e:chota-nagpur-plateau|Chota Nagpur]] hills and came under British supervision around 1818 with the other states taken from the [[s:nagpur-kingdom|Nagpur Kingdom]]. Its ruler was deprived of the state in the 1850s, and it was regranted to a branch of the Sarguja family in 1860.
udaipur-state-chhattisgarh.r: The state was hilly, forested and largely Adivasi, with [[e:kurukh-people|Oraon]], [[e:kawar-people|Kanwar]] and [[e:gond-people|Gond]] communities. It belonged to the [[e:chota-nagpur-plateau|Chota Nagpur]] tributary states and later the [[e:chhattisgarh-feudatory-states|Chhattisgarh States]] group of the [[e:eastern-states-agency|Eastern States Agency]], ruled by a Raja from Dharamjaigarh.
udaipur-state-chhattisgarh.e: [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] acceded to [[e:india|India]] and on 1 January 1948 was merged into the [[e:central-provinces|Central Provinces and Berar]]. Its lands are now in [[s:raigarh-state|Raigarh]] district of [[e:chhattisgarh|Chhattisgarh]].

ubangi-shari.t: The French colony on the Ubangi River that became the Central African Republic, exploited by concession companies.
ubangi-shari.o: French posts along the Ubangi River, including Bangui founded in 1889, were organised in 1903 into the colony of Ubangi-Shari, separate from [[s:gabon-french-colony|Gabon]] and [[s:middle-congo|Middle Congo]]. [[e:chad|Chad]] was attached to it for some years. It formed part of [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]] from 1910.
ubangi-shari.r: Concession companies forced people to collect [[e:rubber|rubber]] and later grow [[e:cotton|cotton]], and thousands were conscripted to build the [[e:congo-ocean-railway|Congo-Ocean railway]] in [[s:middle-congo|Middle Congo]]. The Kongo-[[e:wara|Wara]] rebellion of the [[e:gbaya-people|Gbaya]] from 1928 to 1931 was one of the largest colonial-era revolts. Sultanates such as [[s:sultanate-of-dar-al-kuti|Dar al Kuti]], [[s:sultanate-of-bangassou|Bangassou]] and [[s:sultanate-of-zemio|Zemio]] were absorbed into the administration.
ubangi-shari.e: After 1946 the Catholic priest [[e:barthelemy-boganda|Barthélemy Boganda]] led the nationalist movement. Ubangi-Shari became the [[e:central-african-republic|Central African Republic]] in December 1958 and independent on 13 August 1960, after Boganda's death in an air crash in 1959.

united-states-of-indonesia.t: Federal state to which the Netherlands transferred sovereignty in 1949, dissolved within months into the unitary Republic of Indonesia.
united-states-of-indonesia.o: The [[e:dutch-indonesian-round-table-conference|Round Table Conference]] at [[e:the-hague|The Hague]] in 1949 ended the Indonesian revolution with a compromise. On 27 December 1949 the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] transferred [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] to the Republic of the [[e:united-states|United States]] of [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]], a federation of sixteen states that joined the revolutionary Republic of [[e:indonesia|Indonesia]] with states set up by the [[e:dutch|Dutch]], such as [[e:state-of-east-indonesia|East Indonesia]] and [[e:state-of-pasundan|Pasundan]].
united-states-of-indonesia.r: [[e:sukarno|Sukarno]] became president and [[e:mohammad-hatta|Mohammad Hatta]] prime minister under a federal constitution, linked to the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] in a loose union. Many Indonesians saw the Dutch-created states as colonial puppets, and the attempted coup by [[e:raymond-westerling|Raymond Westerling's]] [[e:american-popular-revolutionary-alliance|APRA]] forces in [[e:bandung|Bandung]] in January 1950 discredited federalism further.
united-states-of-indonesia.e: One by one the member states voted to merge into the Republic, and on 17 August 1950 the federation was replaced by the unitary [[s:indonesia|Indonesia]]. Resistance in the South [[e:maluku-islands|Moluccas]], which proclaimed a separate republic, was suppressed.

umeta-state.t: A minor chiefship on the Mahi river in central Gujarat, one of the small estates of the Rewa Kantha country.
umeta-state.o: Umeta was a small estate on the Mahi river, held by a local chiefly family from around 1600. Its origins are poorly documented.
umeta-state.r: The ruler held a handful of villages and paid tribute to the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]]. In the British period it was grouped among the minor states of the [[e:rewa-kantha-agency|Rewa Kantha Agency]]. Little else is recorded.
umeta-state.e: Umeta was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

usan.t: An island state on Ulleungdo in the East Sea, conquered by Silla in 512 in a famous episode involving wooden lions.
usan.o: Usan, centred on the island of [[e:ulleungdo|Ulleungdo]], appears only in Korean chronicles. Nothing is known of its founding; its people probably lived by fishing and small-scale farming on the volcanic island.
usan.r: The [[e:samguk-sagi|Samguk sagi]] describes its inhabitants as fierce and confident in their isolation, but records nothing of its rulers or institutions.
usan.e: In 512 the [[s:silla|Silla]] general [[e:isabu|Isabu]] sailed to Usan with wooden lions on his ships and threatened to release them unless the islanders surrendered; they submitted and paid annual tribute. [[e:korea|Korea]] later cited Usan in claims to nearby islets.

uzbekistan.t: The most populous Central Asian state, heir to Samarkand and Bukhara, which opened up after decades of Islam Karimov's authoritarian rule.
uzbekistan.o: The [[s:uzbek-ssr|Uzbek SSR]] declared independence on 31 August 1991 under [[e:islam-karimov|Islam Karimov]], who had led the republic since 1989 and was elected president in December 1991. [[e:timur|Timur]] was promoted as a national hero in place of [[e:vladimir-lenin|Lenin]].
uzbekistan.r: [[e:islam-karimov|Karimov]] ruled harshly for 25 years, suppressing opposition and Islamist movements; in 2005 security forces killed hundreds of protesters in [[e:andijan|Andijan]]. The state kept tight control over [[e:cotton|cotton]] production, which relied on forced labour, and over currency exchange. Uzbekistan borders all other Central Asian states and [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]], and the [[e:islamic-movement-of-uzbekistan|Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan]] fought the government from bases abroad.
uzbekistan.e: After [[e:islam-karimov|Karimov]]'s death in 2016, [[e:shavkat-mirziyoyev|Shavkat Mirziyoyev]] became president, freeing some political prisoners, ending forced labour in the [[e:cotton|cotton]] harvest, liberalising the currency and improving relations with neighbours. A 2023 constitution extended presidential terms.

united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg.t: A union of Lower Rhine duchies formed in 1521 whose succession crisis of 1609 brought Europe to the brink of war.
united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg.o: [[e:john-iii-duke-of-cleves|John III]] of [[e:kleve|Cleves]]-Mark married Maria, heiress of Jülich, Berg and [[s:county-of-ravensberg|Ravensberg]]. On his father-in-law's death in 1511 and his own father's in 1521, he united the [[s:duchy-of-julich|Duchy of Jülich]], the [[s:duchy-of-cleves|Duchy of Cleves]] and the [[s:duchy-of-berg|Duchy of Berg]] with the counties of Mark and Ravensberg, ruling from [[e:dusseldorf|Düsseldorf]].
united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg.r: [[e:john-iii-duke-of-cleves|John III]] and his adviser [[e:konrad-von-heresbach|Konrad von Heresbach]] pursued a moderate, Erasmian church policy. The duchies were rich in textiles, iron and [[e:rhine|Rhine]] trade, and the court was a centre of humanism. John's daughter [[e:anne-of-cleves|Anne of Cleves]] married [[e:henry-viii-of-england|Henry VIII of England]] in 1540, and his son [[e:william-duke-of-julich-cleves-berg|William the Rich]] lost [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]] to [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] in 1543.
united-duchies-of-julich-cleves-berg.e: The mentally ill Duke [[e:john-william-duke-of-julich-cleves-berg|John William]] died childless in 1609, setting off the [[e:war-of-the-julich-succession|War of the Jülich Succession]] between [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]]. The [[e:treaty-of-xanten|Treaty of Xanten]] in 1614 divided the lands: [[e:kleve|Cleves]], Mark and [[s:county-of-ravensberg|Ravensberg]] went to Brandenburg, and Jülich and Berg to [[e:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]].

ui-chennselaig.t: Ruling dynasty of south Leinster, based at Ferns, that produced Diarmait Mac Murchada, whose alliance with the Anglo-Normans changed Irish history.
ui-chennselaig.o: The Uí Chennselaig, 'descendants of [[e:enna-cennselach|Énna Cennselach]]', emerged in the 5th and 6th centuries as the leading dynasty of southern [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]], in modern [[e:county-wexford|Wexford]] and [[e:county-carlow|Carlow]]. Their royal centre and church were at [[e:ferns|Ferns]], founded by St [[e:maedoc-of-ferns|Máedóc]]. They competed with the [[e:ui-dunlainge|Uí Dúnlainge]] of the north for the kingship of the Kingdom of Leinster.
ui-chennselaig.r: [[e:brandub-mac-echach|Brandub mac Echach]], who defeated the high king at [[e:battle-of-dun-bolg|Dún Bolg]] in 598, was their most famous early king. After a long period of northern dominance, [[e:diarmait-mac-mael-na-mbo|Diarmait mac Máel na mBó]] revived their fortunes in the 11th century, taking [[e:dublin|Dublin]] and ruling much of southern Ireland. The family of his descendants, the [[e:macmurrough-dynasty|Meic Murchada]] or MacMurroughs, became the kings of [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]].
ui-chennselaig.e: [[e:diarmait-mac-murchada|Diarmait Mac Murchada]], driven out in 1166, brought [[e:anglo-normans|Anglo-Norman]] knights to Ireland. On his death in 1171 [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Strongbow]] took [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]]. The [[e:macmurrough-dynasty|MacMurrough Kavanaghs]] later revived as independent lords in [[e:county-wexford|Wexford]] and [[e:county-carlow|Carlow]], resisting English rule until the 16th century.

udaipur-state.t: Mewar, the Rajput kingdom of the Guhila and Sisodia dynasty, famous for its long resistance to the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals and for the lake city of Udaipur.
udaipur-state.o: The [[e:guhila-dynasty|Guhila dynasty]] emerged in southern [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]] in the 6th to 8th centuries; tradition makes [[e:bappa-rawal|Bappa Rawal]], who held [[e:chittor-fort|Chittor]] in the early 8th century, the true founder. After [[e:alauddin-khalji|Alauddin Khalji]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] sacked Chittor in 1303, [[e:hammir-singh-of-mewar|Hammir Singh]] of the [[e:sisodia|Sisodia]] branch recovered it around 1326, and his line ruled until 1949.
udaipur-state.r: The [[e:maharana|Maharanas]] ruled with powerful [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] nobles who held estates for military service. [[e:rana-kumbha|Rana Kumbha]] built [[e:kumbhalgarh|Kumbhalgarh]] and the Victory Tower at [[e:chittor-fort|Chittor]], [[e:rana-sanga|Rana Sanga]] led the Rajput coalition defeated by [[e:babur|Babur]] at [[e:battle-of-khanwa|Khanwa]] in 1527, and [[e:maharana-pratap|Maharana Pratap]] fought [[e:akbar|Akbar]] at [[e:battle-of-haldighati|Haldighati]] in 1576. [[e:udai-singh-ii|Udai Singh II]] founded [[e:udaipur|Udaipur]] in 1559, and Mewar's court was a centre of painting and temple building.
udaipur-state.e: [[e:amar-singh-i|Amar Singh I]] accepted Mughal overlordship in 1615 on honourable terms, and in 1818 Mewar signed a treaty with the British. In 1948 [[e:bhupal-singh-of-udaipur|Maharana Bhupal Singh]] joined the [[s:united-state-of-rajasthan|United State of Rajasthan]] and became its [[e:rajpramukh|Rajpramukh]]; it became part of [[e:united-state-of-greater-rajasthan|Greater Rajasthan]] in 1949. The city palace and lakes remain major landmarks.
